title: UPDATE 1-Lebanese pound ends unchanged, cbank  intervenes .
text:
BEIRUT, March 1 (Reuters) - Lebanon's pound came under renewed pressure on Tuesday after the surprise resignation of the government under popular pressure unsettled investors already jittery over the killing of an ex-prime minister.  

Traders said the central bank was intervening heavily to maintain the pound at the weakest end of its intervention band of 1,501-1,514 against the dollar. But it closed unchanged.  

"There is a lot of demand against the dollar today. People are worried that the government's resignation has left a political vacuum," said one Lebanese trader.  

"They have to begin consultations for a new government that is neutral and acceptable quickly. If a solution is on the way it will be all right. If not, it is a problem."  

Lebanese officials began looking for a new premier after the Syrian-backed government resigned on Monday following two weeks of protests.  

But it was not clear how long it would take to form a new cabinet and whether the lineup would calm a market already shaken by the killing of Rafik al-Hariri, whom Lebanon's business community considered the country's best hope for economic revival.  

Traders were reluctant to say how much the central bank had spent propping up the pound. It spent over $800 million in total in the first three sessions after Hariri's death, they said, but pressure quickly eased.  

One trader estimated the central bank had spent $400-$500 million, about the same as the first day after Hariri's death, but others said the pressure was lower. Dollar demand also tends to rise at month-end in Lebanon.  

"There was demand but it is not all about the government," said a trader. "There is the end of month factor. Many accounts are blocked until the end of the month, so it is usually busier."  

The central bank promised after Hariri's assassination to defend the pound and keep interest rates unchanged.  

Traders say the central bank has enough gross foreign exchange reserves - $11.4 billion in mid-February - to keep the pound stable for the time being.  

Lebanon's commercial banks, which hold much of the country's public debt equivalent to $33 billion, are also highly liquid, their assets far exceeding gross domestic product.  

But some fear the central bank may have to raise interest rates should pressure be prolonged.  

"The cabinet resignation may be a good thing but the market does not like uncertainty. The central bank has enough reserves but they are not infinite," said another trader at a large Lebanese bank.  

"Either the risk has to fall or the interest rate has to go up. Things need to happen quickly with this new government."

title: Lebanon  pound steady below  intervention  band.
text:
BEIRUT, April 16 (Reuters) - Lebanon's pound hovered just below the bottom end of the central bank intervention band in the week ending Friday as banks who bought special CDs on a forward deal kept dollar demand up, traders said.  

The pound was trading at 1,514-1,516 pounds to the dollar in interbank trade, just outside the 1,501-1,514 band, as banks bought dollars to pay for special high-yielding certificates of deposit that require banks to sell dollars to the central bank.  

Traders said the central bank had offered dollars but mainly to satisfy commercial demand, significant in a country that relies heavily on imports.  

"With reserves this high and the government committed to defending the pound, there is no pressure," said one dealer. "These are just the technical effects of the CDs." The limited offer officially ended months ago but traders said some banks had reached special arrangements to buy up the CDs, which offered yields of 12 percent compared to nine percent usually, on a forward deal.  

The CDs have helped boost foreign currency reserves that had slipped over the past two years as the central bank defended the pound, which came under pressure as fears mounted over the government's ability to service its $30 billion debt.  

The pound had lifted after a 2002 debt aid summit to ease Lebanon's servicing burden briefly raised market confidence.  

But the currency has since slipped as promised reforms, including the long-awaited privatisation of the mobile phone sector, have been delayed by political deadlock.  

Markets were closed Monday and Tuesday for Easter.

title: Lebanon pound hovers below band on regional upset.
text:
BEIRUT, March 26 (Reuters) - Lebanon's pound hovered just below the central bank intervention band in interbank trade this week as concern over Middle East tensions crept into the market, dealers said on Friday.  

They said the pound was changing hands at 1,514-1,516 to the dollar in interbank trade, just outside the weakest end of the 1,501-1,514 band. Officially the band was trading at 1,514.  

"There is a bit of tense situation, political and regional," said one dealer. "But there is still no pressure on the pound. There's just not much offer on the dollar."  

Dealers said the central bank was intervening to the tune of $7-10 million a day, but there was no rush.  

Regional tensions rose this week after Israel killed Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, founder of the militant Palestinian Hamas group, drawing widespread criticism and vows of revenge.  

Lebanese Hizbollah guerrillas retaliated with attacks on Israeli positions in a disputed border area. An Israeli air strike also killed two Palestinians trying to fire rockets into Israel from south Lebanon.  

Dealers said the effects of a special high-yielding CD offer, which required banks to sell dollars to the central bank, were also lingering in the market.  

The central bank stopped the offer, which had boosted its foreign currency reserves, last year but some banks had bought the certificates of deposit on a forward deal.  

The central bank stopped the CD offer in October and resumed treasury bill auctions, which it had suspended for nine months after receiving about $4 billion in soft loans from international lenders in 2002 to help ease its debt service.  

The pound strengthened after that debt aid summit but has since slipped as the government has failed to make good on long-delayed privatisations pledged to lenders at the time.

title: Lebanon's pound steady outside band on CD option.
text:
BEIRUT, Nov 21 (Reuters) - Lebanon's pound was steady outside the central bank intervention band this week as banks who bought special CDs on a forward deal boosted dollar demand, traders said on Friday.  

The pound hovered around 1,516-1,517 to dollar, just outside the 1,501-1,514 band, as banks bought dollars to pay for the special high-yielding certificates of deposit that require banks to sell dollars to the central bank.  

The limited offer officially ended last month but traders said some banks had reached arrangements with the central bank to buy up the CDs, which offered yields of over 12 percent compared to nine usually, on a forward deal.  

"The banks will probably be buying dollars to give to the central bank for the next three or four months for these CDs," one trader said. "This is an artificial level for the pound. It is not because people are giving it up."  

The CDs helped boost foreign currency reserves that had slipped over the past two years as the central bank defended the pound, which came under pressure as fears mounted over the government's ability to service its $30 billion debt.  

Lebanon stopped issuing the special CDs last month and resumed treasury bill auctions, which it had suspended for nine months after receiving about $4 billion soft loans from international lenders to help ease its debt service last year.  

The pound strengthened after that debt aid summit but has since slipped as the government has failed to push ahead with long-delayed privatisations pledged to lenders at the time. ($1=1,507.5 Lebanese pounds).

title: Lebanese pound unshaken by Hizbollah killing.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 8 (Reuters) - Lebanon's pound trod water well inside the central bank intervention band this week, apparently unshaken by the killing of a Hizbollah guerrilla group member, traders said on Friday. They said the pound was trading at about 1,512-1,513 to the dollar, off the weakest end of the 1,501-1,514 intervention band. The interbank rate was steady at about four percent. "The mood is in favour of the pound because the interest rate spread is attractive," said one trader. "The bombing did not affect the currency at all. This shows the pound is not being badly hit by politics." 

 A member of Lebanon's Hizbollah group was killed on Saturday by a bomb planted in his car. Hizbollah blamed Israel and vowed revenge. 

 The Syrian and Iranian-backed group attacked Israeli troops in a disputed border area on Friday, drawing Israel air raids on Lebanese border villages. The Lebanese pound has been affected by domestic political spats and regional upheaval in the past, but traders said the market had largely discounted such risks. 

 Lebanon's pound had come under severe pressure over the past two years as fears mounted over the government's ability to service the roughly $30 billion public debt, forcing the central bank to sell dollars to defend the currency. 

 The pound rose after a debt aid summit late last year, which drew $4 billion in cheap loans to help Lebanon cope with the debt burden. The currency has been further boosted in recent weeks by an influx of tourists from the oil-rich Gulf.

title: Lebanon to probe laundering charges at troubled bank.
text:
BEIRUT, July 11 (Reuters) - A Lebanese prosecutor plans to probe possible money laundering and check fraud by officials at Bank al-Madina, court sources said on Friday, in the latest step to secure deposits at the troubled bank. 

 Rising speculation that the small Beirut bank could not meet its commitments rattled local markets in February, forcing the central bank to step in to reassure depositors. 

 Recent Lebanese media reports said the central bank had frozen accounts of some bank officials to ensure it meets outstanding obligations of more than $200 million to depositors. 

 The prosecutor's probe is expected to bolster government efforts to protect the bank's depositors. 

 Bank sector sources said on Friday the central bank had appointed a temporary manager for Bank al-Madina and an affiliated institution, United Credit, after its existing management failed to make good on obligations to depositors. 

 Representatives of the temporary administrator, contacted at the bank's offices, declined to elaborate on the status of its assets, obligations or accounts. 

 No immediate comment was available from the central bank. 

 The latest developments involving Bank al-Madina did not appear to be unsettling the local currency markets, although they raised the prospect of instability in the country's financial sector - long a haven for Arab investors and an affluent Lebanese diaspora due to its tradition of banking secrecy. 

Lebanon's central bank has periodically intervened in the the administration of troubled banks, injected capital into them or provided soft loans to encourage their acquisition by stronger banks in order to keep the sector stable.

title: Lebanese pound firms as Paris lender meet nears.
text:
BEIRUT, Nov 15 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound strengthened against the dollar in the week ending Friday in the run-up to a lenders' conference that Lebanon hopes will garner up to $5 billion in low-cost loans, traders said. 

 They said the pound was trading around 1,513 pounds to the dollar, near the weaker end of the central bank's 1,501-1,514 intervention band. 

Lebanon will seek the long-term loans at a Paris meeting scheduled for November 23 that it hopes will help reduce the interest burden on its $29 billion public debt, expected to hit 173 percent of gross domestic product by year-end. 

 This second Paris meeting will follow a previous session that generated pledges of about 500 million euros of assistance. 

 "Everybody is waiting. They are thinking it is too good to be true," one dealer said. "After Paris 2 happens, the (dollar) offers will be bigger. I think we will go toward the lower end in the band, but it will take time." 

 Fears about the country's ability to service the debt have put pressure on the currency over the last two years, often forcing the central bank to defend it. 

 But traders said the bank was buying hard currency all week, shoring up its reserves as a rise in confidence boosted the Lebanese currency and reduced demand for dollars. The interbank rate was steady at eight percent. 

 Lebanon also hopes an austere 2003 draft budget, as well as revenue from value-added tax, broader income tax and the sale of mobile phone licences and a stake in the electricity monopoly will help ease the debt burden. 

 ($1=1,507.5 Lebanese pounds).

title: UPDATE 1-Byblos says agrees to buy ABN in Lebanon.
text:
BEIRUT, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Lebanon's Byblos Bank has agreed to buy out the local operations of Dutch bank ABN AMRO in a $36 million cash deal, Byblos chairman Francois Bassil said on Saturday. 

 "There is some fine tuning on the contract, but we agreed on everything," Bassil told Reuters. "We are on the eve of signing." 

 He said Byblos would take over banking operations for ABN AMRO in Lebanon pending approval of the deal by the central bank, adding that ABN AMRO had six branches in Lebanon with around $600 million in deposits and $300 million in loans. 

 Bassil said the deal after several months of negotiations would expand Byblos' product base and portfolio in a market where "good assets are not easy to get". 

 "ABN AMRO is very well established in Lebanon with high quality personnel and risk portfolio," he said. 

 Faced with a sluggish economy, Lebanon's monetary authorities have been intervening to force Lebanon's more than 60 banks to merge or raise their capital adequacy levels. 

 Bassil said that Byblos, with about $400 million in total equity, could easily finance the deal. But he added that Byblos was also planning to increase its capital by up to $150 million through the issue of preferred shares. 

 "We are pre-launching the issuing of $50 to $150 million in preferred shares," he said, adding the issue was also subject to central bank approval. 

 He said he expected the shares to be issued in December or early January. 

 SEEKING MORE ACQUISITIONS 

 Asked if Byblos was still looking for more acquisitions, Bassil said: "Yes, we are looking for others." 

 He said the bank was currently in talks with a medium-sized bank in the region but "outside of Lebanon". 

 "We are in negotiations," he said, adding that he expected talks to take several more months to complete. 

 He added that Byblos had not yet decided whether it was interested in actually acquiring the other bank or doing a joint venture. He declined to give further details. 

 "We haven't fixed the way to do it. We are still in discussions," he said. "We are not in a hurry because we have to digest what we have now. But this is digestible easily, this one." 

 In addition to ABN AMRO, Byblos acquired investment bank ING Barings' Lebanon assets last year for an undisclosed amount. It also bought Wedge Bank in a deal market sources estimated was worth $23 million. 

 Byblos posted close to flat net income last month of 48.7 billion Lebanese pounds ($32.3 million) for the first nine months of 2002. 

 The profitability of Lebanese banks, which finance most of the country's $29 billion public debt, has been slowing as the economy has stagnated. 

 Many banks are adopting cautious lending and currency positions amid concern over state finances, to which they have significant exposure through treasury bill purchases. ($1=1,507.5 Lebanese pounds).

title: Lebanese pound steady ahead of Francophone meet.
text:
BEIRUT, Oct 11 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound traded steady in the week ending Friday ahead of a Francophone conference dealers say they hope will pave the way for a donor meeting that could bring Lebanon financial support. 

 They said they hoped the conference would give Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and French President Jacques Chirac the opportunity to work out the details of the Paris meeting, expected later this year. 

 Lebanon is hoping the Paris meeting of potential donors will help it borrow more cheaply and rein in a mounting public debt. 

 "It (financial support) is on the way," one dealer said. "During the Francophonie, Hariri and Chirac will have a clear idea for Paris 2." 

 Dealers said the pound was trading around 1,513-1,514 pounds to the dollar, at the weaker end of the central bank's 1,501-1,514 intervention band. 

 They said the central bank was selling small amounts of dollars to support the pound amid slightly increased dollar demand, but one dealer called the intervention "minimal". Lebanon's currency has come under increasing pressure as concern has mounted in recent years over the government's ability to handle the country's public debt, expected to hit 178 percent of gross domestic product by year-end. 

 The government is hoping that planned sales of state assets such as mobile licences, as well as tighter public finances, will help it handle a $29 billion public debt. 

 The government is also counting on Gulf Arabs to direct their tourism and investments to Lebanon after the September 11 attacks on the United States. 

 Pressure on the pound fell in May after foreign investors, believed to include Malaysia and Gulf Arab states, bought over $500 million of Lebanese Eurobonds to raise the level of foreign currency reserves at the central bank.

title: Lebanon cbank says completes $3 bln debt swap.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 21 (Reuters) - Lebanon's central bank said on Wednesday that it had swapped 4.5 trillion Lebanese pounds ($2.985 billion) of 2002 paper for debt maturing in 2004, the most recent in a series of swaps to manage a hefty public debt. 

 Lebanon is struggling to service a $29 billion debt run up in reconstruction from its 1975-1990 civil war which is expected to reach 178 percent of GDP by the end of the year, and has placed heavy pressure on the currency over the last two years. 

 The country is converting high-yielding local currency debt into relatively cheap forex-denominated paper, and in May the central bank said it had managed to sell $950 million of its 2005 Lebanon Eurobond holding. 

 In a statement, central bank governor Riad Salameh said the swaps had been made possible by improved sentiment in local currency markets, where the bank has often had to intervene to maintain the Lebanese pound. 

Lebanon is counting on revenue from state asset sales and a new value-added tax, as well as tighter spending, to help it rein in the debt and eventually be able to borrow more cheaply on international capital markets.

title: Lebanese pound steady on progress in mobile sector.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 9 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound remained firm in the week ending Friday as traders said progress towards an agreement with cellular phone operators aimed at privatisation of the sector improved sentiment in the market. 

 Dealers said the pound was trading around 1,512-1,513 pounds to the dollar on the interbank market, well within the central bank's intervention band of 1,501-1,514. 

Lebanon's cabinet approved a proposal on Thursday to offer cellular phone operators Cellis and LibanCell $36-$38 million each to run the sector ahead of privatisation, key to handling a $28.8 billion public debt. 

 Plans for a sell-off have been slowed by government infighting. 

 "They are obliged to arrive at a solution for the cellular phones," said one trader, who saw the decision as one step toward resolving the government squabbling. 

 Mobile revenues are set to revert to the state at the end of the month as a step toward privatising the sector, which has been the site of long-running legal battles between the operators and successive Lebanese governments. 

 Traders said demand for the dollar remained low, and that the central bank, Banque du Liban, was buying dollars. 

 They said they expected the pound to stay at current levels for the rest of the summer without intervention. Overnight interbank rates were also steady at around eight percent. 

 Lebanon's central bank has tapped its reserves to prop up the pound over the past two years as fears mounted about Lebanon's ability to service its public debt, expected to reach 178 percent of GDP this year. 

 In the short term, the government hopes a conference of potential donors that France has offered to host can provide relief in the form of long-term low-interest loans. Dealers said optimism over that conference was also helping the pound. 

 Pressure on the pound fell in May after the central bank said it sold some $950 million of a sovereign Eurobond holding, helping replenish foreign currency reserves. 

 The central bank said gross forex reserves were $4.49 billion at end-July, down from about $7.6 billion in early 2000. The bank does not reveal net hard currency reserves, which most analysts believe are significantly lower. 

 ($1=1,507.5 Lebanese pounds).

title: Lebanon says to seek long-term loans at aid talks.
text:
BEIRUT, July 3 (Reuters) - Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri said on Wednesday he hoped to obtain longer-term loans with lower interest rates at a conference of rich nations in Paris later this year. 

 "We hope to get from Paris financial means to obtain loans to replace the current short-term loans...with longer term loans of 10 to 15 years with lower interest," he told a banking conference on Wednesday. 

 France has said it will host the meeting to discuss lending financial support to Lebanon, which has public debt of around $28 billion, more than 165 percent of gross domestic product. 

 Much of the debt was run up during the decade after the 1975-1990 civil war due to the heavy cost of rebuilding the shattered capital Beirut. 

 Hariri has said he hoped the meeting could take place before the end of the year. Leading Gulf states, the members of the Group of Eight industrialised nations, the European Union and leading international organisations would take part. 

 Hariri also said on Wednesday he had no plans to devalue the Lebanese pound, which has been under increasing pressure as fears about the country's debt rise. 

 "We have no intention to devalue our currency. We think it is bad for the economy and we don't see any benefit for the Lebanese or the economy in general," Hariri said. 

Lebanon's pound trades in a central bank intervention band of 1,510-1,514 to the dollar. 

 "If we devalue the currency..., the interest rates will jump and it will be followed by high inflation, which will hurt the Lebanese," he added. 

 Hariri said he was also concerned a devaluation would hurt the "credibility" of the country, and said it would be unfair to Lebanese who have kept their money in pounds.

title: UPDATE 2-Bank of Beirut says buys Beirut Riyad.
text:
BEIRUT, May 30 (Reuters) - Bank of Beirut, one of Lebanon's top 10 banks, has bought medium-sized Beirut Riyad Bank, officials of both banks said on Thursday, in a deal involving a share transfer but no cash. 

 "It is a done deal," said an official of Bank of Beirut. "Beirut Riyad is now fully owned by Bank of Beirut," the official said. 

 Talks on the deal were first reported by banking sources early this month. 

 An official at Beirut Riyad Bank, which has been asked by monetary authorities to improve its asset quality and raise capital, confirmed the news, saying that it would involve a transfer of shares. 

 "This had to happen or Beirut Riyad would have been forced to find a capital increase," he said, adding that the deal was signed on Wednesday. 

 Beirut Riyad, which has $760 million of assets, has not declared profits for three years because its earnings went to loan provisioning. 

 The bank, which is partly owned by Saudi investors, has 12 branches, including one in London. 

 Doubtful loans comprised 150 billion Lebanese pounds ($99 million) out of 487.3 billion pounds in total loans in 2001. 

 Bank of Beirut has been expanding under new management since the mid-1990s. In 1997, it bought Transorient Bank, a Lebanese bank. Emirates Bank International bought a stake in Bank of Beirut the same year. 

 Bank of Beirut's share on the Beirut Stock Exchange was unchanged at $7.81 on the news. 

 FORCED CONSOLIDATION 

 Analysts said the buyout will swell Bank of Beirut's branch network and is a logical move for the largely retail-based bank. 

 "It will boost the size of the bank and its market, which is what they're after," said one London-based analyst. "That makes sense given that organic growth is difficult in the current environment." 

 Habib Haddad, head of treasury at Beirut Riyad, said the buyout was "good news for both banks." 

 Faced with a retreating economy and rising bad loans, the monetary authorities have been intervening to force Lebanon's 67 banks to merge or raise their capital adequacy levels. 

 The central bank routinely enourages banks to merge by extending them soft loans and the Bank of Beirut official confirmed that his bank would recieve such a loan, although he did not disclose the amount. 

 Bank profits have also been sliding as falling confidence in the government's ability to control a public debt equivalent to more than 165 percent of gross domestic product has put pressure on the currency. Lebanese banks have a high exposure to sovereign risk through large treasury bill holdings. 

 According to the central bank, doubtful loans rose to more than 12 percent of total loans at the end of last year compared to 10 percent in 2000. 

 "Given Beirut Riyad's problems, Bank of Beirut probably didn't have to splash out, but it's hard to tell if this is financially a good deal until we know what arrangements have been made for doubtful loans," said the analyst. "And whether more bad loans are lurking in the background."

title: Cellphone truce keeps Lebanon pound stable.
text:
BEIRUT, May 17 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound was stable in the week ending Friday, as traders said a truce in a government row over a telecoms privatisation that is a key to plans for handling crippling public debt reassured the market. 

 However, they said the central bank remained the only supplier of dollars on the market as overnight interest rates fluctuated at a relatively high 11-15 percent. Overnight rates usually hover around seven or eight percent. 

 The Lebanese pound changed hands at 1,514 to the dollar, the upper limit of the central bank's intervention band of 1,501-1,514 pounds to the dollar. 

 Pressure on the currency has mounted in recent weeks during a row between the president and prime minister over a planned sale of two cellular phone licences the government hopes will raise revenue to help handle its $27 billion public debt, which is expected to reach 178 percent of GDP by yearend. 

 The feuding leaders agreed this week on a broad plan to either auction those licences or rights to operate their networks by the end of August. 

 "The market calmed a bit once a deal was reached," said one dealer, adding that any relief for the currency would ultimately depend on pushing ahead with those sales. 

 "Only progress in privatisation can really ease the pressure," he said. 

Lebanon's central bank has been intervening to prop up the currency as public finances sour, seeing its gross forex reserves drop from the equivalent of $7.6 billion at the end of 2000 to $4.6 billion by mid-April. It does not disclose net hard currency reserves, which are thought to be much lower. 

 The bank raised deposit reserve requirements last year in a bid to give itself more space to defend the currency, and last month hiked interest rates on two-year t-bills to 16.14 percent from 14.14 percent in an attempt to lure people to the pound. ($1=1,507.5 Lebanese pounds).

title: Lebanon 's c.bank  intervenes  to defend pound.
text:
BEIRUT, March 1 (Reuters) - The Lebanese central bank supported the pound this week, selling dollars to maintain the interbank rate at 1,514 pounds to the dollar, the top of its intervention band of 1,501-1,514 to the dollar. 

 The pound has come under increasing pressure over the past year as fears mount over the government's ability to service a public debt that tops 165 percent of GDP. 

 The bank's gross forex reserves fell 20 percent in 2001 but were stabilised at the equivalent of $4.9 billion in the first half of February. 

 Traders said the market was waiting for evidence that a 10 percent value added tax introduced last month was helping repair government finances. 

 The government expects VAT to raise $500 million this year and plans to sell unprofitable state assets to finance a projected budget deficit of $2.5 billion in 2002. 

 "We hear that some privatisation plans are nearly ready and this should bring some cash to the treasury and reduce the pressure (on the currency)," said one dealer. 

 Traders have warned that investors are increasingly unwilling to take on pound assets despite attractive interest rate spreads compared to dollar holdings. 

 Lebanon offers a 14 percent yield on its longest-term treasury bill.

title: Lebanon  cbank  intervention  eases after reform steps.
text:
BEIRUT, Feb 15 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound was stable in the week ending Friday, as traders said a series of economic reform measures calmed the market and allowed the central bank to reduce intervention to defend to pound. 

 They said the currency spent much of the week at the top of the central bank's intervention band of 1,501-1,514 to the dollar, but that the bank's intervention was less extensive than it has been recently. 

 "There was some demand for dollar this week, but the central bank is meeting that demand," said one dealer. "It's definitely less than last week." 

 Fears about Lebanon's ability to service a public debt that tops 165 percent of GDP have squeezed the currency, leaving the central bank the sole source of dollars for much of last year, and cutting gross reserves to the equivalent of $4.85 billion by end-January from some $5.9 billion at end-2000. 

 The bank does not disclose net forex reserves, and expresses gross reserves as a Lebanese pound figure. 

 Traders said pressure on the pound eased after introduction of a 10 percent value added tax that the government hopes will help repair its finances and a cabinet decision this week to cancel commercial monopolies that contradict a new economic partnership accord with the European Union. 

 But dealers said there was a limit to market confidence, noting that investors are increasingly unwilling to take on pound assets, despite attractive interest rates spreads compared to dollar holdings. 

 Lebanon offers a 14 percent yield on its longest-term treasury bill, a rate traders say has moved investors back into local currency following a series of interest rate cuts by the U.S. Federal Reserve last year. 

 "From time to time some people still temporarily sell dollars and hold pounds, but there are fewer and fewer of them and more and more of those holding dollars," one dealer said.

title: Lebanon pound stable, cenbank on sidelines.
text:
BEIRUT, Jan 11 (Reuters) - Lebanon's central bank reduced its intervention in the market to maintain a stable exchange rate this week after demand rose for the Lebanese pound , dealers said on Friday. 

 They said the interbank exchange rate remained unchanged at 1,514 pounds to the dollar and the Banque du Liban stopped offering a 16 percent yield on Lebanese pound bonds instead of 14 percent to create demand for the pound. 

 Dealers said even without the premium offered by the central bank on the bills, the spread on pound holdings compared to dollars was high enough to create demand for the currency. 

 "If the central bank sold dollars, it was in very small quantities," said a dealer at a large bank. 

 Wadih Sabbagh, chief dealer at Byblos Bank, said the pound had started 2002 on a better note. 

 "We have clients who switched significant deposits to the pound. But they are freezing them for short periods - three months at most," Sabbagh added. 

 He expected pressure on the pound to resume if the government did not secure international assistance to control the public debt and did not work hard to streamline and sell loss-making state enterprises. 

 A public debt that exceeded 160 percent of gross domestic product last year has lessened confidence in the pound and forced the monetary authorities to defend it, by buying treasury bills and offering premiums to those already in the market. 

 The bank also has sold dollars from its reserves, which fell 20 percent to $4.72 billion at the end of 2001. 

 In a research note Banque Audi said that central bank holdings of Lebanese pound treasury bills had risen to 6,000 billion (about $4 billion) by the end of 2001. ($1=1,508 Lebanese pounds).

title: Lebanese pound stable despite Argentine crisis.
text:
BEIRUT, Dec 21 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound remained stable this week despite the Argentine crisis and a similar high level of public debt in Lebanon, dealers said on Friday. 

 They said readiness by the monetary authorities to provide the market with liquidity and attractive 14 percent yields on Lebanese pound treasury bills maintained stability in the market. 

 The interbank exchange rate remained steady at 1,514 pounds to the dollar - the upper end of the central bank's intervention band. 

 "There was no knock on effect in Lebanon," said a bond trader at a large bank. "It was restricted to some of the few foreigners holding Lebanese Eurobonds. They exited weeks ago." 

 Emerging market debt have been pushed lower by Argentina's eminent default on $132 billion of debt and what appears to be inevitable devaluation of its currency. 

 Local banks hold most of Lebanon's $26 billion public debt, equivalent to more than 160 percent of gross domestic product. The banks, which also account for most of the $4.3 billion of gross foreign currency reserves at Banque du Liban, have held to Lebanese bonds in times of pressure. 

 Risk of government default have put pressure on the Lebanese pound and forced the central bank to provide the market with dollars from its reserves, which were $5.9 billion at the beginning of year. 

 "A solution must be found to control the debt. We are not seeing anything concrete," another dealer said.

title: Lebanese pound remains steady, eyes on politics.
text:
BEIRUT, Dec 7 (Reuters) - Lebanon's pound was steady against the dollar in quiet trade this week, as the market looked ahead to a cabinet meeting on a set of politically charged government appointments, dealers said on Friday. 

 They said the pound was trading off the top of the central bank's intervention band of 1,501-1,514 to the dollar at 1,513 during most of the week, with banks reversing the trend of much of the year and selling hard currency to the central bank. 

Lebanon's central bank has intervened heavily to defend the pound this year, as fears about the country's ability to service a public debt of $26 billion, equivalent to more than 160 percent of GDP, undermine confidence in the currency. 

 Dealers said the the pound, which local investors dump for hard currency at any sign of political strife, would take its cue next week from a Tuesday cabinet meeting at which a set of hotly contested administrative appointments will be made. 

 "The political climate is not that bad, but we still have Tuesday to overcome. If it goes smoothly, there are better days ahead of us," said a currency trader at a major Lebanese bank. 

 Among the appointments the cabinet is set to discuss is the top job at the country's loss-making electricity company, which the government hopes to privatise to decrease its debt burden. 

 The cabinet meeting was scheduled after Lebanon's energy minister last week accused the head of the company - which collects only half its bills - of exacerbating power cuts in order to embarrass the government, and demanded he be sacked. 

 Sales of state assets including utilities and cellular phone operating licences are a key to Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri's plan to slow the growth of the debt, which eats up the bulk of government revenue and chokes off growth. ($1=1,508 Lebanese pounds).

title: Calm returns to Lebanese pound after U.S. row.
text:
BEIRUT, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound was steady this week as calm returned to the market following a recent political dispute with the United States over money laundering, dealers said on Friday. 

 They said the exchange rate was stable at near the upper end of Banque du Liban's intervention band of 1,514 pounds to the dollar with supply of hard currency coming from within the market. 

 "The spreads are in the pound's favour. They are overshadowing the disagreement with Washington and encouraging depositors to switch to the local currency," said Nabil Chaya, head of treasury at Banque Audi, said. 

 The central bank intervened briefly in the market last week after Lebanon refused a U.S. demand to seize the assets of the Hizbollah guerrilla group. Washington said it would consider taking retaliatory action against Lebanese banks. 

 The banks do a large proportion of their business in or through the United States. Their health is crucial to the governments strategy of defending the pound. 

 The banks buy most of Lebanon's $26 billion public debt and contribute significantly to foreign currency reserves. 

 The central bank has increased demand for the pound with swap operations that raised the yield on the benchmark two-year treasury bill to 16 percent compared to the two percent federal funds rate. 

 Financiers said monetary authorities were buying time and that the government had to make reforms and succeed in receiving international support to control the debt. 

 Wadih Sabbagh, chief dealer at Byblos Bank, expected investors to switch to the pound as Lebanese banks start cutting interest rates on dollar deposits from 5-6 percent to 4.5-5.5 percent in response to the U.S. cuts. 

 "The interest rates differential is the main factor driving the market at present," said Sabbagh. 

 ($1=1,507.5 Lebanese pounds).

title: UPDATE 1-Lebanon reserves fall to $4.146 bln at end August.
text:
BEIRUT, Sept 3 (Reuters) - Lebanon's gross foreign currency reserves fell to 6.251 trillion Lebanese pounds ($4.146 billion) at the end of August from 6.838 trillion pounds in mid-August, the central bank said on Monday. 

 Reserves stood at about $4.77 billion at the end of July compared with about $5.9 billion at the end of 2000 and $7.6 billion at the end of 1999. The reserve figure includes deposits by commercial banks and state agencies. 

 Bankers attributed the fall to a political storm that swept the country when the army arrested 200 members of Christian opposition groups in a crackdown against those opposed to Syrian influence in Lebanon. 

 The arrests sparked a feud between pro-Syrian President Emile Lahoud and Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri who said his government had not been informed about the move. Politicians warned that cabinet had been handcuffed and that Lebanon was in danger of becoming a dictatorship run by Syria. 

 "Lebanon lost millions of dollars because of the differences between officials while the country needs every dollar to face the huge public debt," a banker told Reuters. 

 Political tensions have taken their toll on the Lebanese pound on whose behalf the bank has intervened heavily to support. 

 They have also compounded anxiety about Lebanon's 25 billion public debt, which exceeds 155 percent of GDP, huge budget deficit and doubts about whether the government can deal with the problem at a time of zero economic growth. 

 "The big fall of reserves is a warning to Lebanese officials to put their differences aside and deal with the political and economic problems facing their country," the banking source, who requested anonymity, added. 

 Both Lahoud and Hariri mended fences at the end of last month after the army released most detainees but investors' confidence has yet to be restored. 

 Syria has some 20,000 troops and hundreds of thousands of workers in Lebanon. Their presence rankles with many Lebanese, particularly Christians, who resent Syria's domination of Lebanese politics. 

 The central bank, which traders say is generally the only seller of hard currency locally, does not disclose net reserve levels. 

 ($1 = 1,507.5 Lebanese pounds since September 1999).

title: Politics compounds pressure on Lebanon pound.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 17 (Reuters) - Pressure mounted on Lebanon's ailing currency this week as political tension added to anxiety over the country's massive debt and weak finances, traders said on Friday. 

 They said the pound traded at the top of the central bank's intervention band of 1,501-1,514 to the dollar, as a feud between the cabinet and Lebanon's pro-Syrian president over a crackdown on dissidents opposed to Syria's political domination of the country boosted dollar demand. 

 "There was heavy dollar demand due to what happened, and the central bank was the only provider of dollars," said a currency trader with a major Lebanese bank. 

 Lebanese security forces last week rounded up about 200 Christian dissidents who want Syria to withdraw its 20,000 troops from Lebanon. 

 The cabinet said it had not been informed of the crackdown beforehand, leading opposition politicians to warn that government had been handcuffed and that the country is in danger of becoming a military dictatorship run by Syria. 

 The political tensions have compounded anxiety about Lebanon's $24 billion public debt, which exceeds 155 percent of GDP, huge budget deficit, and doubts whether the government can handle either problem while the country experiences virtually zero economic growth. 

Lebanon's central bank, which has intervened heavily to maintain the exchange rate for months, this week said its gross foreign currency reserves were $4.5 billion, compared to about $5.9 billion at the end of 2000. 

 The bank has also reported falling subscriptions in each of the last several t-bill auctions. This week said it sold no certificates of deposit. 

 The International Monetary Fund warned last month that local banks, long the main consumers of government debt, are recording slower deposit growth and may not be able to meet the government's financing needs. 

 Lebanon's government hopes to whittle down the public debt through a combination of politically sensitive spending cuts and sales of unwieldy state assets.

title: Lebanon pound squeezed as dollar demand stays high.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 10 (Reuters) - Pressure on the Lebanese pound stayed high this week, with the central bank the only seller of dollars, forex dealers said on Friday. 

 "Nobody's selling (dollars) at all. It's a one-way market," said a trader with a large Lebanese bank, who said the pound had traded at the upper limit of the central bank intervention band of 1,501-1,514 against the dollar. 

Lebanon's central bank intervenes in the currency market heavily to defend the currency, which has been undermined by fears about the country's $24 billion public debt, stagnant economy and volatile southern border with Israel. 

 The government of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri is vowing to sell state assets to help whittle down the debt but faces stiff political opposition to planned redundancies at state firms and cuts in a budget bloated by political patronage.

title: Beirut banks eye fee business as loan, debt risk high.
text:
BEIRUT, August 7 (Reuters) - Lebanon's banks will turn to retail services and other fee-earning business to help make up for conservative lending policies forced on them by the country's economic woes, bankers and analysts said on Tuesday. 

 Many of the country's leading banks reported stagnant or falling first-half profits, and said that macroeconomic pressures were forcing them to adopt conservative lending strategies to reduce the ratio of bad loans in their portfolio. 

 The Lebanese government, with debt of over $24 billion or about 155 percent of GDP, is facing mounting pressure on the currency while it turns to politically sensitive plans for fiscal reform and privatisation to cope with the debt and end several years of recession. 

 Local banks, meanwhile, are major holders of Lebanese pound-denominated debt, whose prices would drop with a devaluation. While reducing lending, they are seeking to draw income from retail services, such as processing payments of mobile phone and utility bills and offering Internet bank accounts and services, said a strategist for one bank. 

 "(The sector) is focusing on non-interest income and fee earning business, which is not affected as much by the economic sluggishness," said Marwan Barakat of Banque Audi , whose first half profits fell 9.5 percent year-on-year to $16.5 million. 

 Fellow leading bank Blom said cutting doubtful loans allowed it to increase first-half profits slightly from the previous year to $39.48 million, while Byblos Bank said conservative investment strategies helped bring its first-half profits down 7.8 percent year-on-year to $24 million. 

 An executive of one bank who asked not to be identified said the banking sector, traditionally a magnet for deposits from Lebanese living abroad and from Arab investors, was not crawling inside its shell completely but sought to manage its risk. 

 "Essentially it's your still-traditional approach of trying to lend as much as possible with good risk in the private sector," he said. 

 The International Monetary Fund last month warned Lebanese authorities that a slowing growth in the deposit base of local banks suggested a looming crisis in their ability to finance the government's borrowing needs. 

 Banks have extended their wariness of risk to debt denominated in pounds, while Lebanon's central bank has been intervening in the market heavily for months to prop up prices, the unidentified banker said. 

 "In the central bank's balance sheets you're seeing a big rise in T-bills (purchases), because the last few issues have not been fully subscribed. It indicates increasing awareness of the risk," he said.

title: Lebanon cenbank remains main supplier of dollars.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 3 (Reuters) - Demand for U.S. dollars was limited in the Lebanese market this week, with the central bank the main supplier of the hard currency, dealers said. 

 "There is limited demand and very few suppliers other than the central bank," one dealer said. 

 They said the local unit was unchanged at the upper end of the central bankintervention band of 1,501-1,514 Lebanese pounds to the dollar. 

Lebanon's central bank has been intervening for months to defend the pound, which has been undermined by worries about $24 billion of public debt as well as tension on the country's southern border between Hizbollah guerrillas and Israel.

title: Lebanon pound pressured at top of cenbank band.
text:
BEIRUT, July 27 (Reuters) - Pressure on the Lebanese pound stayed high this week, with the central bank the main supplier of dollars to the forex market, dealers said on Friday. 

 "We've seen some sales of dollars for working capital purposes, but nothing on a major scale," said a dealer at one large bank. He said the pound traded at the top of the central bank's intervention band of 1,501-1,514 against the dollar. 

Lebanon's central bank has been intervening for months to defend the currency, which has been undermined by anxiety about the $24 billion of public debt and military tension on the southern border between Hizbollah guerrillas and Israel. 

 The government of Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri has vowed to sell state assets to help whittle down the debt, but faces opposition from state employees and an uphill battle to streamline unwieldy companies like the state power concern.

title: Business as usual in Lebanon despite Mideast tensions.
text:
BEIRUT, Oct 12 (Reuters) - The currency is under pressure, state finances are shaky and many do not rule out war, but the Lebanese flair for doing business continues unscathed. 

 In a country were hotels and factories went up in the midst of the 1975-1990 civil war and banks kept operating from blast-proof rooms, the violence the Middle East is currently witnessing pales by comparison. 

 "It's silly to say that people are not a bit edgy, but (property) business is going on almost as usual," said Raja Makarem, head of real estate consultancy Ramco. 

 Makarem said he was arranging a 20-year lease for a new shopping centre and the $10 million sale of a bank building in downtown Beirut. 

 "The mall deal is being finalised and the other buyer is still strongly interested in the bank building," said Makarem. 

 "A slowdown is inevitable, many people will wait and see, but Lebanon will not lose its resilience," he added. 

 The Israeli withdrawal from south Lebanon in May helped the real estate market recover from a sharp decline. There has been renewed interest in downtown Beirut, which is nearly monopolised by Solidere, the largest firm in the country. 

 Property was the main destination of foreign capital inflows after the end of the civil war. Some foreign investors are still reluctant to enter the market without peace between Lebanon and Israel. But others have no such qualms. Three Saudi businessmen are currently going ahead with a $70 million hotel on the Beirut seafront. 

 POSITIVE SPIN 

Lebanon's central bank has been forced to intervene to keep the exchange rate stable and has spent at least $160 million this week to defend the currency, according to dealers, who said depositors were switching their bank accounts to dollars. 

 But the newly changed dollars would be invested in Lebanese assets, said Habib Haddad, head of treasury at Bank Beirut Riyad. 

 He said the newly found dollar liquidity would be mostly invested in Lebanese eurobonds, which fell this week. The Republic's 2009 bond lost $1 and its spread rose by 40 basis points to 440. 

 "There was no significant selling of bonds and they dropped on low volume," Haddad said. 

 He said Lebanon has never defaulted on its sovereign debt, which are mostly held by local banks, and the country has managed to launch eurobonds in the bleakest of times, such as during the 1998 Asian crisis and during the recent tensions. 

 "In no time they found on Wednesday takers for a 250 million euros ($200 million) in an addition to their existing Eurobond," Haddad said. 

 On October 25 a new fund linked to Lebanese eurobonds and arranged by Bank of Beirut will be launched. Officials said a presentation to international investors is going ahead.

title: Lebanon foreign reserves down $14.9 mln in mid-Apr.
text:
BEIRUT, April 18 (Reuters) - Lebanon's gross foreign reserves fell $14.99 million to $7.253 billion in mid-April from $7.268 billion at the end of March, the central bank said on Tuesday. 

 Gross foreign reserves, which include deposits by commercial banks and government agencies, were $7.352 billion in mid-March. 

 Bankers last week said the Bank of Lebanon intervened in the foreign exchange market for the first time in almost a year, selling dollars to shore up the pound. 

 Lebanon ended 1999 with gross reserves of $7.61 billion compared to $6.41 billion in 1998 and $5.93 billion in 1997. 

 The central bank does not disclose net reserves.

title: INTERVIEW-Lebanese c.bank lowers GDP forecast.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 24 (Reuters) - Central Bank Governor Riad Salameh on Tuesday forecast Lebanon's economy to grow in 1999 by around one percent and said there would be virtually no inflation due to the slowdown. 

 Salameh had previously expected gross domestic product to increase by between two and three percent this year and inflation to hover around the three percent mark. 

 "Based on the performance of the past seven months, we've changed our estimates (of GDP growth) so that it's closer to one percent. If activity gets better it might rise to two percent," he told Reuters by telephone. 

 According to government figures, GDP growth in 1998 was around three percent. 

 This year a contraction in investment and demand, estimated by Lebanon's leading Banque Audi at four percent and caused by the government's austerity measures, has driven the economy into recession. 

 The Banque Audi report said that a GDP growth of two percent required an increase in local and international demand to about $900 million, a figure the bank said would be near impossible to achieve in the second half of the year. 

 Tax and customs increases, part of the government's 1999 budget and five-year economic reform plan, have also contributed to the slowdown, which Salameh said would partially drive inflation to near zero percent. 

 He had earlier forecast a 2.5 percentage point rise in inflation this year due to the government's new tax policy. 

 In April, the government raised duties on income, corporate profits, imports, alcohol, tobacco and gasoline. The taxes aim at increasing revenues by 2.5 percent from 1998 levels to 4,990 billion pounds ($3.31 billion) and curbing the budget deficit to 40.5 percent from 43.6 percent a year ago. 

 "Our firm monetary policy has also contributed to reducing inflation," Salameh added. "It's below our five percent ceiling and also below the three percent we forecast earlier." 

 The Bank of Lebanon manages the pound by an official intervention band of 1,508 to 1,514 pound to the dollar. Salameh has said he would cause the pound to appreciate if inflation crossed the five percent mark. 

 But changing the exchange rate is currently far from Salameh's mind. Dollar supply in the Lebanese foreign exchange market has been plentiful over the past two months, during which the central bank bought around $450 million, he said. 

 "The market is anticipating lower rates and a stable pound which is why investors are shifting away from dollars. Also, they are locking in treasury-bill yields," he added. 

 The central bank has recently slashed interest rates on Lebanese pound paper, mainly two-year treasury bills which now yield 15.36 percent compared to about 16 percent a few weeks ago. Yields on one-year treasury bills have also been falling steadily and are now at 14.77 percent.

title: Lebanon  forex  market calm despite violence.
text:
BEIRUT, May 7 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound traded calmly in the week ended on Friday despite a flare-up of violence in south Lebanon, dealers said. 

 "There was nothing in the market. Demand for dollars was very little with also little supply. Interbank operations reached about $28 million," a dealer said. 

 One trader said Lebanon's central bank did not intervene in the market because there was no pressure on the pound, despite Israeli warplane raids into southern Lebanon almost every day this week in retaliation against attacks by pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas. 

 Another dealer said interbank rates were steady at last week's range of 1,512.50-1,5013.5 for the dollar. 

 The range was inside the central bank's bid-offer intervention band which has stood at 1,502-1,514 since mid-October when army commander Emile Lahoud was elected president. 

 Dealers also blamed the stagnant market on the still outstanding 1999 budget, which is being discussed in parliament. 

 Last week, the central bank sold $6 million to $7 million in the market compared to $20 million a week earlier. 

 ((Beirut newsroom +9611 745 306/8 fax 745 336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Lebanon cen.bank supports pound in dull market.
text:
BEIRUT, April 30 (Reuters) - Lebanon's central bank sold dollars this week to meet thin demand for the U.S. currency in a stagnant but tight foreign exchange market, dealers said. 

 "The market was stable this week. There was light demand for dollars but there was no supply so the central bank sold $6 million to $7 million," one dealer said. 

 Dealers said light demand kept the interbank dealing range at 1,512.50-1,513.50 pounds to the dollar, which is on the upper range of the central bank's bid-offer intervention band. 

 The Bank of Lebanon has kept the band steady at between 1,502 and 1,514 pounds to the dollar since mid-October when army commander Emile Lahoud was elected president. 

 Violence in the south, where Israel occupies a 15 km (nine mile) wide zone, and economic indicators had put a damper on the market, the dealer said. 

 "Investors see the tense situation in the south on one hand and the government's decision to start collecting donations and its budget on the other hand and they've decided to halt their investments," he said. 

 This week, seven Israeli soldiers, three pro-Israeli South Lebanon Army militiamen and three civilians were wounded in south Lebanon fighting. 

 The government on Wednesday decided to establish a fund for Lebanese emigrants to collect contributions while a parliamentary committee started discussing the 1999 budget bill, which targets a deficit of 40.2 percent. 

 "Who will be encouraged to invest in a country that is collecting donations?" another dealer said. 

 The central bank supplied the market with $20 million a week ago and with $50 million a week earlier. 

 ((Beirut newsroom +9611 745 306/8 fax 745 336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)). 

 (C) Reuters Limited 1999.

title: Lebanese  central bank  sells dollars to support pound.

 "The market was very calm this week. There was light demand for dollars but there was no supply so the central bank sold about $20 million," a dealer said. 

 The dealer said after Israel annexed the village of Arnoun to its south Lebanon occupation zone last week investors feared further Israeli military actions ahead of parliamentary elections in the Jewish state scheduled for May 17. 

 The previous week the central bank supplied the market with $50 million. 

 Another dealer said light demand for dollars kept interbank dealing on the upper edge of the central bank bid-offer intervention band, which has been steady at 1,502-1,514 pounds to the dollar since mid-October when army commander Emile Lahoud was elected president.

title: Lebanese  central bank intervenes  in  forex  market.
text:
BEIRUT, April 8 (Reuters) - Lebanon's central bank intervened in the foreign exchange market this week for the first time in over a month, injecting around $30 million to ease mounting demand pressures for the U.S. currency, bankers said. 

 "Demand on the dollar rose in the start of the week. The central bank intervened, selling about $20 million on Tuesday only," said one banker who requested anonymity. 

 Another banker said demand for the dollar had eased later in the three-day working week. He also said the government's announcement of its 1999 budget figures had little effect on the forex market. 

 "The budget did not really affect the market. It caused the demand to continue yet it was a smaller demand than that we saw at the beginning of the week after the Hariri issue," said another broker. 

 Political pressure mounted last week on former premier and billionaire Rafik al-Hariri who is blamed for spending beyond the country's financial means. At the end of his six-year term Lebanon's debt reached $18 billion. 

 The four-month-old government of Prime Minister Selim al-Hoss on Wednesday announced its 1999 draft budget with a deficit of 40.2 percent of spending, down from 43 percent last year. 

 The interbank trading ranged between 1,513-1,514 Lebanese pounds to the dollar compared with last week's range of 1,508-1,511 pounds. 

 The central bank range was steady at 1,502-1,514 pounds. 

 The market was closed until Tuesday for Easter. Thursday is the last working day before another four-day public holiday. 

 ((Beirut editorial (9611) 745 308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Dlr demand wanes in Beirut, investors await budget.
text:
BEIRUT, March 19 (Reuters) - Pressure on the Lebanese pound continued to ease this week in a lifeless foreign currency market which dealers said was awaiting the 1999 budget. 

 They said the pound "comfortably" traded within the official band set by the Bank of Lebanon, making central bank intervention in the market unnecessary. 

 The central bank has been largely supplying the market with dollars since December to prevent the pound from moving outside a range that has stood at between 1,502 pounds and 1,514 pounds to the dollar so far this year. 

 One dealer, who put the total size of the market at $50 to $60 million, said the lack of intervention by the central bank should not be interpreted much as a very positive sign. 

 "The market is completely frozen. The mood is lingering ahead of the budget," he said. 

 Investors have been waiting to see the 1999 budget and the government's efforts to reduce a deficit that finished at around 14 percent of GDP last year. The budget was due by the beginning of March but has been delayed. 

 ((Beirut editorial (9611) 745 308 fax 745336

title: Lebanese presidential choice caused rush to pound.
text:
BEIRUT, Oct 9 (Reuters) - Agreement on naming the head of the army as Lebanon's next president caused a rush into the Lebanese pound from U.S. dollars in the week ended on Friday, dealers said. 

 "The heavy supply of dollars in the market this week made the central bank intervene, buying about $135 million," one dealer said. 

 "This supply reflected the atmosphere of confidence in the near-term political future of the country," he said, echoing the feeling among other dealers feeling that a smooth transition to a new president would ensure stability. 

 Another dealer said: "The Turkish-Syrian crisis made some people hestitate in getting rid of their dollars, otherwise the supply of the American currency would have been much higher. 

 "Investors shifted towards Lebanese-pound denominated treasury bills," he added. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer official intervention band stood in the range of 1,502.50-1,515.50 Lebanese pounds per dollar against Friday's 1,503.00-1,516.00 - the usual appreciation set by the government. 

 Interbank trading stood on the lower edge of the central bank's bid-offer intervention band in the range of 1,502.40-1,502.60 from 1,503.00. 

 Earlier this week Syria, the main foreign power broker in Lebanon, backed army commander Emile Lahoud as the next president and on Thursday the Lebanese cabinet asked parliament to amend the constitution to pave Lahoud's way to the presidency. 

 Syria keeps 35,000 troops in Lebanon. They originally entered to help to restore order during the 1975-1990 civil war. 

 Regional tension rose this week when Turkey threatened Syria over its alleged support for the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK). 

 ((Beirut editorial (9611) 745308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)). 

 (C) Reuters Limited 1998.

title: Lebanese pound gains as political tension eases.
text:
BEIRUT, Oct 2 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound gained against the U.S. dollar this week as political tension over the presidential election eased, dealers said on Friday. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer intervention band stood in the range of 1,503.00-1,516.00 against 1,503.50-1,516.50 last week, the standard rate of appreciation maintained by the central bank. 

 "Contacts made by Lebanese officials abroad and the defusing of political tension related to the presidential election was behind the relaxed atmosphere in the market," a dealer said. 

 "Supply and demand for U.S. currency were balanced on the first two days of the week. But supply outpaced demand in the rest of the week and the central bank intervened, buying about $40 million," another dealer said. 

 Interbank trading stood at 1,503.00 Lebanese pound for one dollar from a range of 1,505.50-1,507.50 in the first two days of the week against last week's 1,511-1512. 

 Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri headed Lebanon's delegation to the United Nation's General Assembly meeting last month in New York where his contacts included talks with World Bank officials. 

 Lebanon's first presidential election since the 1975-1990 civil war had raised concerns in the market in recent weeks, but the political rhetoric subsided this week. The vote is to take place this month and is seen a test of the country's stability. ((Beirut editorial (9611) 745308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)). 

 (C) Reuters Limited 1998.

title: Central bank  helps Lebanese pound in quiet market.
text:
BEIRUT, Sept 11 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound made gains with the help of central bank intervention in a quiet market in the week ended on Friday, dealers said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer intervention band stood in the range of 1,504.50-1,517.50 compared with 1,505.00-1,518.00 last Friday. 

 "There was some commercial demand for U.S. dollars with little supply but the market was quiet," said a dealer who requested anonymity. 

 "This week, the central bank sold between $35 million and $40 million to support the pound," the dealer said. 

 Another dealer said the demand for the U.S. currency was due to market anxiety over presidential elections due to be held next month. 

 "Some investors prefer to wait until the presidential elections are over before they involve themselves in any new Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bills," another dealer said. 

 Lebanon is planning to have presidential elections in October. 

 The dealer said he expected Lebanon's successful placement of $350 million of new debt on international markets on Thursday to boost confidence in the country, 

 "The placement of the bond issue took place on Thursday. So we have to wait for next week to see its results. But I think this issue represents a renewal of the international community's confidence in Lebanon," he said. 

 Interbank trading stood at 1,517.50-1,518.00 against last week's 1,517.75-1,518.25, he added. 

 ((Beirut editorial (9611) 745308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Bank of  Lebanon intervenes  to help pound.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 21 (Reuters) - Lebanon's central bank intervened in the currency market to ease pressure on the Lebanese pound in the week to Friday, dealers said. 

 "There was some demand for the U.S. dollar because of various reasons such as the buying of dollars ahead of presidential elections," said a dealer who requested anonymity. 

 Lebanon is planning to hold presidential elections in October. The Beirut market is highly sensitive to political tensions. 

 Interbank trading stood at 1,518.50-1,519.50 Lebanese pounds for a dollar against last week's closing level of 1,519.50-1,520.00. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer intervention band was in the range of 1,506.00-1,519.00 Lebanese pounds for the dollar compared to last week's 1,506.50-1,519.50. 

 In recent weeks, relations between Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri have been tense. 

 But the dealer said those political problems have not had an impact on the Lebanese pound over the last week. 

 ((Beirut editorial (9611) 745308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Lebanon political tension boosts USD demand.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 14 (Reuters) - Political uncertainty boosted demand for U.S. dollars in the week ending on Friday and the central bank intervened to sell the U.S. currency to ease pressure on the Lebanese pound, dealers said. 

 "The central bank sold up to $25 million in the last two days to support the Lebanese pound," a dealer said. 

 Interbank trading climbed over the upper edge of the central bank bid-offer intervention band closing on Friday at 1,519.50-1,520.00 for a dollar against last week's range of 1,509.50-1,512.50, he said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer intervention band stood at 1,506.50-1,519.50 Lebanese pounds for the dollar compared to last week's 1,507.50-1,519.50. 

 Another dealer attributed the high demand for dollars to rising political tension. "The political tension still affects the market very much," he said. 

 Tension surfaced in July over differences between political leaders on a number of issues including a new salary scale for the public sector and uncertainties over planned presidential elections in October. 

 (Beirut editorial (9611) 745-308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Lebanese pound official rate up against dollar.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 7 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound posted new gains against the U.S. dollar in the week to Friday, but the greenback gained some ground against the local currency in interbank dealings, dealers said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer intervention band stood at 1,507.50-1,519.50 Lebanese pounds for the dollar compared WITH last week's 1,508.00-1,520.00. 

 Dealers attributed gains in interbank dealings to rising political tension. 

 Tension surfaced early in July as differences among political leaders over a number of issues, including a new salary scale for the public sector, and uncertainties over planned presidential election in October, came into the open. 

 Interbank trading closed on Friday at 1,512.5-1,509.50 to the dollar against last week's range of 1,508.00-1,508.15.

 He said demand exceeded supply towards the end of the week. 

 "Offers emerged on Monday and the central bank intervened, buying about $8.0 million," he said, adding that market turnover reached some $50 million. ((Beirut editorial (9611) 745-308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Lebanese pound faces pressure, then recovers.
text:
BEIRUT, July 31 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound faced a bout of mid-week pressure because of increased political tension, dealers said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer intervention band stood at 1,508.00-1,520.00 Lebanese pounds for a dollar compared to last week's 1,508.50-1,520.50 - the rate of appreciation set by the government in the past couple of years. 

 "The market was quiet at the beginning of the week. But under the impact of the political confusion we witnessed some artificial demand (for dollars) on Wednesday and Thursday," a dealer said. 

 "On Friday, supply of the U.S. currency was much more than demand and the central bank bought about $8.0 million. The total volume of the market this week was about $50 million," the dealer said. 

 Interbank trading was 1,508.00-1,508.15 for a dollar against last week's range of 1,508.25-1,508.50, he said. 

 The powerful Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri and Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri this week accused each other of violating the constitution. It reflected tension in advance of a presidential election expected in October. 

 (Beirut editorial (9611) 745-308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Lebanese pound continues to gain against dollar.

BEIRUT, July 24 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound continued to gain against the U.S. dollar, with the central bank intervening to buy dollars in the week ended on Friday, dealers said. 

 "There was some supply of dollar and the central bank was buying the U.S. currency in a range of $5.0 million to $15 million per day," a dealer, who asked for anonymity, told Reuters. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer intervention band stood at 1,508.50-1,520.50 Lebanese pounds against the dollar compared to last week's 1,509.00-1,521.00.

title: Lebanese pound boosted by dollar selling.
text:
BEIRUT, May 29 (Reuters) - Lebanon's central bank bought dollars this week amid upward pressure on the Lebanese pound from a rush into local treasury bills, dealers said on Friday. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer intervention band stood at 1,512.50-1,524.50 Lebanese pounds to the dollar compared to last week's range of 1,513-1,525, continuing the steady appreciation of the official rate. 

 But a dealer said the rise this week reflected funadamentals in the market, with investors rushing to buy Lebanese treasury bills and lock in high annual interest rates that have begun to decline. 

 "The central bank was buying dollars on an average of $15 million to $20 million a day in the last two weeks," said another dealer. 

 "We saw a little demand for the dollar from two banks only, probably for some private operations. But this did not influence the trend of supply of the U.S. currency," the dealer said. 

 Interbank trading was in the range of 1,512.60-1,512.75 pounds to the dollar against last week's 1,513-1,513.25, he added. 

 ((Beirut editorial (9611) 745308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: Central bank , quiet Lebanese politics help pound.
text:
BEIRUT, May 22 (Reuters) - Central bank intervention, investments in treasury bills and a quiet political scene ahead of the first local elections in 35 years strengthened the Lebanese pound in the week ended on Friday, dealers said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer intervention band stood at 1,513.00-1,525.00 Lebanese pounds to the dollar compared to last week's range of 1,513.50-1,525.50. 

 Interbank trading was in the range of 1,513.00-1,513.25 pounds to the dollar against last week's 1,513.25-1,513.75. 

 Dealers said the Bank of Lebanon had intervened to help the pound. But they also noted that the pound had made gains because the Lebanese political scene was free of troubles ahead of local elections. 

 On Sunday, Lebanon will hold its first municipal elections in 35 years in a contest that analysts said could pose a challenge to the country's top leaders. 

 "The quiet political situation has helped the pound," said one dealer. 

 Another dealer said banks were buying Lebanese pounds to invest in long-term Lebanese treasury bills, a development that also boosted the Lebanese currency. 

 ((Beirut editorial (9611) 745308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)). 

 (C) Reuters Limited 1998.

title: UAE deposit boosts Lebanese pound in week.
text:
BEIRUT, May 8 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound continued to gain against the U.S. dollar on the three working days of the week ended on Friday, with dealers reporting that a $100 million United Arab Emirates deposit in the central bank boosted the pound. 

 Lebanon's financial markets were closed on Wednesday and Thursday for holidays. 

 The Bank of Lebanon bid-offer intervention band stood at 1,514-1,526 pounds to the dollar on Friday from last Friday's 1,514-1,526.50. 

 Interbank trading was at the lower edge of the central bank intervention band and reached 1,514-1,514.50 Lebanese pounds to the dollar on Friday from last week's 1,515.50-1,516.50, a dealer said. 

 "There was quite a good amount of supply of dollars in the market and the central bank intervened as a buyer for the U.S. currency," the dealer added. 

 Another dealer said the pound was boosted by the restored confidence in Lebanon caused by the $100 million UAE deposit in the central bank and the $1 billion bond issue in March. 

 "There was a supply of dollar this week following reports about the $100 million UAE deposit in the central bank," the dealer said. 

 "The UAE deposit and the previous Saudi and Kuwaiti deposits and the $1 billion Eurobond issue encouraged foreign investors to return to the treasury bills market," he added. 

 On Monday Lebanon said it had reached an agreement with UAE for a $100 million deposit for three years starting May 7. 

 In January, Kuwait deposited $100 million with Lebanon's central bank at five percent interest rate for three years. This followed a Saudi Arabian deposit of $500 million at the same interest rate for three years and $100 million to be spent on investment infrastructure. 

 In March, Lebanon raised $1.0 billion on the international market via two well-received bond issues with five-and three-year maturities. 

 ((Beirut newsroom (9611) 745308 fax 745336 

 beirut.newsroom@reuters.com)).

title: United Arab Emirates Lends Lebanon $100 Million To Shore Up  Currency
text:
BEIRUT -(Dow Jones)- The United Arab Emirates is to lend Lebanon $100 million in order to shore up the Lebanese pound, newspapers reported Tuesday. 

 Newspapers said the loan agreement was signed by the director-general of the Abu Dhabi National Bank, Sheik Mohammed Jarroush el-Sweidi, Lebanon's agriculture minister, Shawki Fakhoury, and the governor of the Bank of Lebanon, Riad Salameh, in Abu Dhabi on Monday. 

 The government is thought to be waiting for the money to enter Lebanon's accounts before announcing the loan. The deposit is expected Thursday. 

 The newspaper As-Safir quoted the central bank's deputy governor, Nasser al-Saidi, as saying the interest rate on the three-year loan was 5%. 

 Saudi Arabia and Kuwait lent Lebanon $600 million and $100 million respectively last year for the same purpose. Those loans were also for three years at 5% interest. 

 The Bank of Lebanon has intervened repeatedly in recent months to defend the pound against speculators on the currency markets. The pound currently trades at 1,520 pounds to the dollar. 

 Prime Minister Rafik Hariri has made it a pillar of his policies to maintain the value of the currency. 

 Financial experts in Beirut see the loans as expressing confidence in the pound.

title: Lebanon central bank intervenes  to support pound.
text:
BEIRUT, Nov 14 (Reuters) - Lebanon's central bank intervened in the currency market to support the pound on Friday amid talk of a possible near-term assault on the local currency, dealers said. 

 "This is what we have been hearing," one dealer said. "But I don't think there will be a catastrophe because the central bank always intervenes to back the pound." 

 The central bank's bid-offer intervention band was 1525.00-1535.00 compared to last week's 1525.50-1535.50. 

 Inter-bank dollar trading was in the range of 1535.00-1535.50 compared to last week's 1535.50-1536.00. 

 The central bank said on Tuesday it was offering to swap Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bills at interest rates well above those on existing finance ministry T-bills. 

 A banking source said the move reflected the central bank's policy of supporting the Lebanese pound, which has come under pressure over the last two months. 

 The central bank had attributed growing pressure on the foreign exchange reserves to the currency crisis in Asia. But Lebanon has also been struggling with a large fiscal deficit that has pushed the level of debt close to the annual gross domestic product.

title: Lebanon  Central Banker/Pound -2:  Intervened  In Sept.
text:
Salameh said that there is some risk of "stagnation" if foreign investors stay out of emerging markets for some time. But "liquidity has to be placed somewhere," and the Middle East, which attracted little institutional money so far, could benefit, he said. 

 Last month, the Lebanese central bank had to buy a substantial amount of Lebanese pounds during a feud among the country's top officials, stemming from a proposed budget plan that would have raised gasoline taxes. 

 Salameh wouldn't specify the exact amount of the bank's purchases, but said the estimates of $1 billion to $1.5 billion mentioned in Lebanese political circles are exaggerated. 

 The Bank of Lebanon has said that its foreign exchange reserves stood at $6.35 billion at the end of September, down $89.37 million from the middle of that month. Mid-October figures are due out Monday. 

 Lebanon's parliament has begun considering a new budget proposal, calling for $800 million in new revenues from increased car-registration fees and other measures.
