title: Demand for dollar eases in Lebanon  forex  market.
text:
BEIRUT, Oct 24 (Reuters) - The Lebanese central bank intervened to support the local pound in the foreign exchange market in the week ended on Friday but demand for the dollar eased, dealers said. 

 "The central bank intervened but not as much as two weeks ago," said one dealer, referring to a period when political tensions raised demand for the dollar. 

 "There were small tensions in the market. But there was not much demand for the dollar. The pound was a little bit stronger," he added. 

 The Bank of Lebanon's bid-offer intervention band was 1526.50-1536.50 compared to last week's 1527.00-1537.00. 

 Inter-bank dollar trading was in the range of 1536.00-1537.00 against last week's 1536.00-1538.50.

title: Lebanese pound gains by end of week on budget hopes.
text:
BEIRUT, Oct 17 (Reuters) - The Lebanese pound gained ground by the close of the week ending on Friday after political leaders put aside their differences over the 1998 budget, dealers said. 

 They said demand for the dollar had eased at the end of the week after Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri ended a dispute over the budget, which still needs parliamentary approval. 

 "At the end of the week the market was much better after the two leaders came to an agreement," said one dealer. 

 The Lebanese pound has been more sensitive to events in the political arena since Hariri's plan to partly finance a controversial $800 million development plan by raising petrol prices was rejected by the cabinet on September 24. 

 Dealers said the Lebanese currency had recovered from the cabinet's decision last week. 

 The Bank of Lebanon's bid-offer intervention band was 1527.00-1537.00 Lebanese pounds compared to last week's 1527.50-1537.50. 

 "The central bank intervened but not that much because demand for the dollar decreased by the end of the week," said another dealer. 

 Inter-bank dollar trading was in the range of 1536.00-1538.50 against last week's 1537.00-1538.50.

title: Lebanon central bank intervenes  on  forex  market.
text:
BEIRUT, Sept 19 (Reuter) - Lebanon's central bank intervened to satisfy demand for the dollar which outpaced supply in the week ended on Friday, dealers said. 

 "There was some dollar supply this week but demand was a little bit higher than that supply and the central bank intervened to satisfy the market," a dealer said. 

 "The demand came from investors who had Lebanese pound denominated treasury bills which matured and were not renewed so they shifted to the U.S. currency," the dealer said. The Bank of Lebanon's bid-offer intervention band was 1529.00-1539.00 pounds against last week's 1529.50-1539.50. 

 Inter-bank dollar trading was in the range 1538.75-1539.25 Lebanese pounds compared to last week's 1539.25-1540.75, the dealer said.

title: Bank of Lebanon  forex  reserves fall in mid-Sept.
text:
BEIRUT, Sept 17 (Reuter) - The Bank of Lebanon's gross foreign exchange reserves fell in the first half of September for the first time in 17 months, dropping $160.44 million to $6.437 billion, the central bank said on Wednesday. 

 Banking sources said the drop in the foreign exchange reserves was mainly because commercial banks withdrew a total of $110.44 million from deposits at the central bank. 

 This was the first drop in the gross foreign reserves of the central bank since the second half of April 1996 when they dropped by $95.67 million to $4.683 billion. 

 On Friday, Central Bank Governor Riad Salameh said the bank would continue to intervene on foreign exchange markets, keeping a narrow bid-offer spread and ensuring a steady appreciation of the Lebanese pound which collapsed during the 1975-90 civil war. 

 Last week, the Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band for the local currency to 1529.50-1539.50 pounds to the dollar against 1530.00-1540.00 a week earlier. 

 Gross reserves had risen by $1.5 million in the second half of August to $6.598 billion. They include commercial banks' net foreign exchange deposits with the central bank. 

 The bank gave no figure for net reserves but banking sources said they dropped to $4.350 billion in mid-September from $4.400 billion at the end of August. 

 According to the banking sources, net reserves stood at $4.015 billion at the end of 1996 compared with $2.858 a year earlier. 

 - Beirut editorial (961 1) 745307 745308 602057

title: Dollar demand steady on  Lebanon  market.
text:

 Inter-bank dollar trading was in a range of 1539.75-1540.25 Lebanese pounds compared to last week's 1539.25-1540.00, the dealers said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon's bid-offer intervention band was 1530.00-1540.00 pounds against last week's 1531.00-1540.00. 

 Dealers said there was steady demand for the dollar throughout the week.

title: Lebanese pound edges up in week.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 29 (Reuter) - Trading in the Lebanese pound remained close to the upper end of the central bank's bid-offer intervention band and the dollar lost ground in the week ended on Friday, dealers said. 

 Inter-bank dollar trading was in a range of 1539.25-1540.00 Lebanese pounds compared to last week's 1540.00-1540.20, the dealers said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon's bid-offer intervention band was 1531.00-1540.00 Lebanese pounds against last week's 1531.50-1540.50. 

 "The dollar was in equilibrium between supply and demand at the start of the week and then demand eased," said one dealer. "Demand eased even though there were problems in the south." 

 Four Israeli troops and four guerrillas of the pro-Syrian Amal Movement were killed in violence in south Lebanon on Thursday, capping the region's bloodiest month in over a year. 

 A dealer said the central bank had intervened on the foreign exchange market but the market had satisfied demand for the dollar. - Beirut editorial (9611) 745307 745308

title: Lebanese pound edges down on week.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 14 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound traded at the upper end of the central bank's bid-offer intervention band in the week ended on Thursday amid continued demand for U.S. dollars on the Beirut foreign exchange market, dealers said. 

 The inter-bank trading of the dollar was in a range of 1541.00-1541.50 Lebanese pounds against last week's range of 1,535.00-1,541.50, dealers said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon's bid-offer intervention band was 1,532.00-1,541.00 Lebanese pounds compared to last week's 1,532.50-1,541.50, continuing the official policy of a slight pound appreciation. 

 Investors who did not renew subscription in Lebanese-pound-denominated treasury bills shifted to dollars, said a dealer, who asked not to be identified. 

 "Demand for dollars was much higher than offer, which was very light because some matured treasury bills were not renewed," he added. 

 Banks and financial markets will close on Friday for the Assumption day holiday.

title: Dollar supply climbs in Lebanon  forex  market.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 1 (Reuter) - The Bank of Lebanon intervened on the Beirut foreign exchange market for the fifth straight week to satisfy dollar demand before supply climbed near the end of the week, dealers said on Friday. 

 The bank's bid-offer intervention band was 1,533.00-1,542.00 over last week's 1,533.50-1,542.50. 

 Dealers said the dollar supply rose after the United States' decision on Wednesday to lift a 10-year-old ban on its citizens travelling to Lebanon. 

 "Before the announcement on the ban there was demand for the dollar and low supply. But afterwards the dollar supply increased," said one dealer. 

 "In the last two days, the dollar was traded between the central bank's range and not at the top of its band because there was a big supply of dollars after the travel ban news," said another. 

 In interbank trading, dealers said the dollar weakened and hit 1,538-1,539 Lebanese pounds by Friday, falling from 1,542-1,542.50 a few days earlier. -- Beirut editorial (9611) 745307, 745308

title: Lebanese cen. bank sells small amount dlrs-dealers.
text:
BEIRUT, July 25 (Reuter) - The Bank of Lebanon intervened on Beirut foreign exchange markets for the fourth straight week to meet demand for the dollar, keeping the price range almost unchanged, dealers said on Friday. 

 The bank's bid-offer intervention band was 1,533.50-1,542.50 Lebanese pounds, indicating a pound marginally stronger than last week's 1,534-1,543. "The bank lowered its price range," said a broker. 

 "There was a little bit of demand for the U.S. currency but not a dangerous amount," said another dealer. "The bank did not sell a lot of dollars." 

 In interbank trading, the dollar edged down to 1,542-1,542.50 Lebanese pounds from last week's 1,542.5-1,543 pounds, dealers said. 

 It was the fourth straight week that the central bank had intervened to satisfy demand for dollars, dealers said.

title: Lebanese pound steady in c.bank's price range.
text:
BEIRUT, July 18 (Reuter) - The Bank of Lebanon intervened on the Beirut foreign exchange for the third straight week to satisfy demand for dollars in the week ended on Friday, selling the dollars for 1,543 Lebanese pounds, dealers said. 

 The bank's bid-offer intervention band was 1,534-1,543 Lebanese pounds against last week's 1,534.5-1,543. 

 Interbank trading, meanwhile, climbed to 1,542.5-1,543 Lebanese pounds from last week's 1,542-1542.75 pounds. 

 "There was demand from banks for dollars. The central bank was selling dollars. There was no change from last week. The market has the same sentiments," said a broker. 

 It was the third week that the central bank has intervened at the top of its bid-offer intervention band to sell dollars, dealers said. 

 Some dealers said the central bank was merely setting a price range to keep market forces at work. 

 "The bank was not intervening. It set a price ceiling and floor in order to keep the dollar steady and let the market play its role," he said. 

 He added that the purchase of dollars was being fuelled by greater investor interest in buying shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange.

title: B.of  Lebanon intervened  in past wk on  forex  market.
text:
BEIRUT, July 11 (Reuter) - The Bank of Lebanon intervened on the Beirut foreign exchange market to meet demand for dollars in the week ended on Friday, selling the dollars for 1,543 Lebanese pounds, at the top of its intervention band, dealers said. 

 The central bank intervened at 1,543 from Monday to Thursday but stopped on Friday when dollar supply reappeared on the market and the pound climbed to 1,542-1,542.75 in interbank trading, dealers said. 

 It was the second week that the central bank has intervened at the top of its bid-offer intervention band to sell dollars. It sold at 1,543-1,543.5 last week. 

 The bank changed the intervention band during the past week to 1,534.5-1,543 from 1,535.5-1,543. 

 "Yesterday and every day before that we were buying dollars at the Bank of Lebanon rate of 1,543 pounds, but today there was a bit of dollar supply on the market so we were dealing below the central bank rate at 1,542-1,542.75," a dealer who asked not to be identified told Reuters. 

 "At the end of the week there were some good signs because I think there is some saturation on the market and there is a supply of dollars," he said. 

 Dealers last week said political problems were causing increased demand for dollars. 

 They cited a civil disobedience campaign launched in eastern Lebanon by a radical Shi'ite cleric, a dispute between President Elias Hrawi and Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri over command of internal security troops and a flare-up of fighting in south Lebanon between Moslem guerrillas and Israeli troops.

title: Lebanon pound falls on political ills-dealers.
text:
BEIRUT, July 4 (Reuter) - The Bank of Lebanon intervened on the Beirut foreign exchange market in the week ended on Friday, selling dollars at the upper limit of its bid-offer intervention band to meet demand for the U.S. currency, dealers said. 

 They said the Lebanese pound fell to 1,543.5 to the dollar on Thursday and the central bank intervened on Friday to buy pounds at 1,543 -- the upper limit of the band. Dealers cited political uncertainties for the trend. 

 The central bank lowered the intervention band during the week to 1,535.5-1,543 pounds per dollar from last week's 1,535.5-1,544. 

 The pound traded in inter-bank trade last week in a range of 1,539-1,542.5. 

 Dealers said there was a small amount of inter-bank trade at prices 25 to 50 piastres below the central bank rate but most of the demand for dollars could not be met by commercial banks. 

 "The central bank intervened and sold dollars in the market. Many banks bought from the central bank," a dealer who asked not to be identified said of this week's trade. 

 "Last week there was a central bank selling price for dollars but the market was below this. This week the market reached the central bank rate and banks bought dollars from it," he said. 

 "Many banks bought dollars directly from the Bank of Lebanon because there was some demand for dollars and no supply because of the political situation," he added. 

 He cited a civil disobedience campaign launched in eastern Lebanon on Friday by a radical Shi'ite cleric, a dispute between President Elias Hrawi and Prime Minister Rafic al-Hariri over command of internal security troops and fighting in south Lebanon between Moslem guerrillas and Israeli troops. 

 "Because of all this there was some tension in the market and demand for dollars," the dealer said.

title: Lebanese pound edges down on week.
text:
BEIRUT, June 27 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound edged closer to the upper end of the central bank's bid-offer intervention band in the week ended on Friday amid continued demand for U.S. dollars on the Beirut foreign exchange market, dealers said. 

 The dollar traded in inter-bank trade in a range of 1,539-1,542.5 pounds compared with 1,538-1,541 last week and 1,536-1,537.5 the week before, they said. 

 This was near the upper end of the intervention band which the Bank of Lebanon lowered during the week to 1,535.5-1,544 pounds per dollar from last week's 1,535.5-1,545. 

 "I think the highest deal during the week was 1,542.5, but 1,543 was the highest price quoted," a dealer who asked not to be identified told Reuters. 

 He said there was some supply of dollars and the market was balanced. 

 "We didn't reach (top end of) the Bank of Lebanon rate. I don't think anyone bought dollars from the central bank," he said. 

 Dealers said last week restrictions of allocations of shorter-term pound-denominated treasury bills by the central bank were helping to boost demand for dollars as investors who were allowed to buy only a small fraction of the bills they bid for changed their excess funds back to dollars. 

 On Friday, dealers said there was no change of trend on the market on which the Lebanese pound has steadily appreciated against the U.S. currency for the past five years. 

 However, the dollar was routinely in over-supply for several months until early June and traded for weeks in a tight range of a few dozen piastres at the bottom of the central bank's intervention rate. 

 Asked why the dollar was now more in demand, a dealer said restrictions on t-bill allocations were still affecting the market and there was some political tension. 

 This appeared a reference to controversy over the government's June 10 decision to raise import duties on cars and ban imports of some food products from October in a bid to reduce the heavy trade deficit and stimulate local agriculture.

title: Bank of Lebanon buys dollars - Governor.
text:
BEIRUT, May 21 (Reuter) - The Bank of Lebanon has bought more than $900 million on the Beirut foreign exchange market since the start of 1997, Governor Riad Salameh said on Wednesday. 

 "The Bank of Lebanon has intervened as a buyer of more than $900 million since the beginning of the year," Salameh told Arab bankers and financiers at a conference in Beirut. 

 The rate of dolarisation of bank deposits fell to 55 percent in April, he added. 

Foreign exchange dealers told Reuters the central bank had consistently bought dollars on the market this year. 

 "There have only been about 20 days on which the Bank of Lebanon did not take dollars from the market," Talal Abou Zaki, forex manager at Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, said. 

 "There are still people offering dollars and switching to Lebanese pounds, and I think there are also outside investors taking advantage of high interest rates on the Lebanese pound who are buying treasury bills," Abou Zaki said. 

 The Lebanese pound has continued its steady appreciation against the U.S. dollar during 1997. 

 It is currently at 1,542.5 to the dollar compared with 1,552 at the end of December 1996. 

 - Beirut editorial (9611) 345723 345740 602057

title: Lebanese pound up on dollar in week.
text:
BEIRUT, May 15 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound continued to rise against the dollar in the week ended on Thursday, and dealers said there was heavy supply of U.S. currency during the the four working days. 

 The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band during the week to 1,538-1,547.5 pounds per dollar from 1,538.5-1,548 and the dollar traded at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said. 

 Shadi Hanna, Treasurer at Byblos Bank, said the dollar's supply was high and trade was restricted to a tight range of 75 piasters at the bid end of the intervention band, putting it at 1,538.25-1,539. 

 Last week the dollar closed at 1,538.5-1,539 pound in interbank trading. 

 "All demand for dollars was met by commercial banks and the Central Bank bought between $5 million to $10 million," Hanna told Reuters. 

 Markets will be closed on Friday for Moslem Ashoura holiday.

title: Lebanese pound firms against dollar.
text:
BEIRUT, April 14 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound regained ground against the U.S. dollar in quiet interbank trade in Beirut on Monday and dealers said the market was calming down after a flurry of activity last week. 

 The market opened at 1,546-1,549 pounds to the dollar from 1,548.5 on Friday, but the Lebanese currency firmed steadily during the morning to 1,543-1,545, a dealer who asked not to be identified told Reuters. 

 The pound moved at the close to 1,545-1,548 per dollar as some banks closed their positions, the dealer added. He estimated trade at $4-$5 million. 

 The Bank of Lebanon's bid-offer intervention band was unchanged from last week's 1,540-1549.5 pounds per dollar. 

 "All trade was within the Bank of Lebanon's intervention rate and there was some selling of dollars by banks due to treasury bill purchases and the Eid al-Adha holiday on Thursday," the dealer added. 

 "I think it is a matter of time before we have a calm market again. There was nothing special today," he said. 

 Last week the pound fell six points against the dollar within the central bank's intervention band in interbank trade as one commercial bank bought a large amount of the U.S. currency, putting pressure on the Lebanese pound. 

 - Beirut editorial (961 1) 345723 345740 602057

title: Lebanese pound eases against dollar.
text:
BEIRUT, April 11 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound fell back against the dollar in interbank trade in the week ended on Friday amid heavy demand for U.S. currency, dealers said. 

 They said commercial banks traded the pound at 1548.5 per dollar -- six pounds stronger than the previous week's interbank rate of 1,542.5 and 2.5 pounds above Thursday's 1,546. 

 The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band during the week to 1,540-1549.5 pounds per dollar from 1,540.5-1,550 last week. 

 Dealers said a large dollar order by one commercial bank created pressure at the beginning of the week. 

 "Demand for dollars continued as a result of political uncertainty arising from the issue of municipal elections," Nabil Abou Jaoude, Treasury and Forex manager for Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce told Reuters. 

 The government's withdrawal of the elections bill last week angered President Elias Hrawi, Christian and leftist opposition and caused concern that the government might delay the elections which are due in June. 

 "Another factor is the restrictions imposed by the central bank on short term treasury bills which led non-resident investors to shift to U.S. currency," he said. 

 Pressure on the market slowed down trading operations on Friday, dealers said. 

 "Despite many questions asked on the market, trade was thin today. It seems everyone was in a wait-and-see state after the bid-offer margin was close to one pound," Abou Jaoude said. 

 All demand for dollars was met by commercial banks without central bank intervention, Shadi Hanna Treasurer for Bank Byblos told Reuters. 

 "The market was very normal and the central bank is in full control. The rise of the U.S. dollar is a technical matter," Hanna said. 

 -Beirut editorial (961 1) 602057 745307 745308

title: Lebanese pound wobbles on political uncertainty.
text:
BEIRUT, April 4 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound initially continued its steady rise against the U.S. dollar for the first three days of the week but fell back slightly in interbank trade on Friday due to political uncertainties, dealers said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band during the week to 1,540.5-1550 pounds per dollar from 1,541-1,550.5. 

 Dealers said commercial banks traded the pound from Tuesday to Thursday after the long Easter weekend at 1,541.5 per dollar -- one pound stronger than the previous week's interbank rate of 1,542.5. 

 However, Thursday's resignation of Constitutional Council chief Wajdi al-Mallat and the government's withdrawal of a bill to amend the municipal elections law sparked increased dollar demand on Friday and the pound fell back to 1,542.5 per dollar. 

 All demand for dollars was met by commercial banks without central bank intervention, dealers said. 

 The withdrawal of the elections bill caused concern among politicians and the media that the government might delay the first local elections since 1963 which are due in June. 

 "Trade among banks was quiet in the first three days of the week at one pound above the bid end of the intervention band," Talal Abou Zaki, Forex Manager for Bank Beirut and the Arab Countries said, "but due to political confusion on Thursday the dollar was traded two pounds above the bid end." 

 "The resignation of the head of Constitutional Council and indications of a postponement of municipal elections had some effect on the currency trade in the market," Abou Zaki said. 

 Mallat resigned amid reports that the Constitutional Council was facing heavy political pressures over appeals it is handling against the results of last year's parliamentary elections. 

 The withdrawal of the elections bill raised expectations of a possible dispute between Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and President Elias Hrawi who has made clear that he opposes any delay in holding the elections. 

 -Beirut editorial (961 1) 602057 745307 745308 

 (c) Reuters Limited 1997

title: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.
text:
BEIRUT, March 27 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound continued its rise against the U.S. dollar in the week ended on Thursday despite heavy demand for U.S. dollars which dealers said was met by commercial banks. 

 The market will be closed on Friday and Monday for the Good Friday and Easter Monday holidays. 

 The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band to 1,541-1,550.5 pounds per dollar from 1,541.5-1,551 and dealers said commercial banks traded the U.S. currency during the week at 1,541-1,542.5 pounds. 

 "The dollar traded in heavy demand among banks at 1.5 pounds above the bid end of the intervention band due to the maturity of the three- and six-month treasury bills that were not renewed by the central bank," Nabil Abou Jaoude, Treasury and Forex manager for Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce said. 

 Foreign investors unable to renew their matured t-bill subscriptions had changed their money back into dollars, Abou Jaoude said. 

 -Beirut editorial (961 1) 602057 745307 745308

title: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.
text:
BEIRUT, March 14 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound continued rising against the U.S. dollar in the week ended on Friday, and dealers said the latest central bank decision to exempt banks from mandatory t-bill subscriptions relaxed the market. 

 The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band to 1,542-1,551.5 pounds per dollar from last week's 1,542-1,552.5, and the dollar traded at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said. 

 Nabil Abou Jaoude, Treasury and Forex Manager at Banque Libanaise pour Le Commerce, said trade was restricted to a tight range of up to 65 piastres at the bid end of the intervention band. 

 There was some demand for dollars, but all was met by the banks, he said. 

 Market sentiment was positively affected by Wednesday's central bank decision to exempt commercial banks from compulsory subscription of 40 percent of their Lebanese pound deposits in treasury bills, Abou Jaoude said. 

 "This decision left a positive psychological influence on the market, and we still await for more relaxing decisions from the central bank," he added. 

 -Beirut editorial (961 1) 602057 745307 745308

title: Lebanese pound continues rise against dollar.
text:
BEIRUT, March 7 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound continued its rise against the U.S. dollar in an active market in the week ended on Friday, and dealers said there was some demand for dollars that was met by commercial banks. 

 The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band to 1,542-1,552.5 pounds per dollar from 1,543-1,552.5 and the dollar traded at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said. 

 Talal Abou Zaki, Manager of Forex and Money market for Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, said trade was restricted to a tight range of 25 to 75 piastres at the bid end of the intervention band. 

 There was some demand for dollars by foreign investors but all were met by the banks without intervention by the central bank, a dealer said. 

 "Foreign investors whose Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bills matured and did not want to buy new bills were demanding dollars, but their demands were met by the banks with no intervention from the central bank," the dealer added. 

 -Beirut editorial (961 1) 602057 745307 745308

title: Lebanese pound continues slight rise on dollar.
text:
BEIRUT, Feb 7 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound continued to strengthen slightly against the U.S. dollar in the week ended Friday in a quiet market despite the heated parliamentary debate on the 1997 state budget, dealers said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band to 1,544.5-1,554 pounds per dollar from 1,545-1,554.5 and the dollar continued to trade at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said. 

 "The heated parliamentary debate did not leave any influence on the market as investors knew that this debate will not affect the budget figures," Talal Abou Zaki, manager of forex and money market for Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, told Reuters. 

 After five days of heated debate, parliament approved on Monday a 6,433 billion pounds ($4.15 billion) state budget for 1997 with a 36 percent deficit of income against expenditure. 

 Abou Zaki said investors are still interested in Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bills as their yields continued to fall. 

 "The trend is still the same, there is dollar offer and pound demand orders because investors see the trend of the Lebanese pound interest rates decreasing," he added. 

 Yields on Lebanese pound-denominated treasury bills continued to fall during the week. They now stand at 13.96 percent for three-month maturities, and 14.98 percent, 15.37 percent and 16.34 percent for six-month, one-year and two-year bills respectively.

title: Exotic  Currency  Focus: Lebanon Pays For Strong Pound
text:
New York (AP-Dow Jones)--High hopes are being pinned on a comprehensive Middle East peace settlement and Lebanon's multi-billion dollar reconstruction program to ensure the continued stability of the Lebanese pound. 

 With the combined economic benefits of a peace agreement and a restored infrastructure, the Bank of Lebanon might be able to abandon its policy of heavy interventions and high interest rates that it has used to support the currency, some analysts said. 

 This in turn could relieve the country's yawning fiscal deficit, a result of spending for reconstruction programs and debt servicing, which some analysts warn is inflationary and could subvert the government's efforts to maintain a stable currency. 

 Suha Najjar, a Middle East analyst at Nomura Research in London, said the central bank isn't expected to relax its monetary policy until the country enjoys greater political and economic stability. 

 The pound has appreciated 18% against the U.S. dollar since the beginning of 1993 and was quoted at a dollar rate of 1550 Tuesday by Banque Saradar S.A.L. in Lebanon. 

 In 1992, as Lebanon was beginning its recovery from a 16-year civil war that left damages estimated at $30 billion, the pound was at a dollar rate of 2,000. 

 Since then, the government of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri has maintained a steadfast policy of strengthening the pound as a means to restoring investor confidence in the post-war economy.

title: Lebanese pound strengthens further during week.
text:
BEIRUT, Jan 17 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound continued its steady appreciation against the U.S. dollar in the week ended Friday on a quiet market with a continued oversupply of dollars, dealers said. 

 The Bank of Lebanon lowered its bid-offer intervention band to 1,546-1,555.50 pounds per dollar from 1,546.5-1,556 and the dollar again traded at the bottom of the band throughout the week, dealers said. 

 The central bank bought most of the dollars on offer and commercial banks absorbed only 15-20 percent, dealers said.

 Trade was limited to a very tight band of 10-25 piastres at the bid end of the central bank's intervention band, Abou Zaki said. 

 After the Bank lowered its bid rate to 1,546 pounds on Tuesday, the dollar traded at 1,546-1,546.25 or 1,546.05-1,546.15, he added.

title: Dollar well offered on Beirut  forex  market.
text:

 The Bank of Lebanon continued its steady reduction of the intervention rate, lowering its offer rate by one Lebanese pound to 1,546.5-1,556 from last Friday's 1,546.5-1,557.

title: Lebanese pound strengthens in quiet market.
text:
BEIRUT, Nov 29 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound strengthened against the dollar in the week ended on Friday with trade confined to a tight 15-25 piastres spread at the bottom of the Bank of Lebanon's intervention band, dealers said. 

 The market was not very active, they said. 

 The central bank twice adjusted its bid-offer intervention band by 50 piastres during the week to reach 1,550-1,558 Lebanese pounds per dollar from 1,551-1,558 at last Friday's close. 

 Political events, including a sometimes hard-hitting parliamentary confidence debate on Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri's new government followed by a partially effective general strike on Thursday against Hariri's policies, had no impact on the market, dealers said. 

 "The political events did not affect the market in the least," a dealer with a Beirut bank told Reuters. "The market was very calm." 

 Most banks ignored Thursday's strike and financial markets including foreign exchange dealers stayed open during the stoppage. 

 One dealer said the pound traded throughout the week at 1,550.05-1,550.20 per dollar and another said the range was 1,550.0-1,550.25. 

 "There was good offer of dollars. People were buying Lebanese pounds. It is all because of the expectation of falling interest rates on Lebanese pound treasury bills," the dealer said.

title: Beirut  forex  market quiet during week.
text:
BEIRUT, Nov 15 (Reuter) - Beirut's foreign exchange market was quiet during the week ending on Friday, with trading mostly confined to a very narrow spread at the lower end of the Bank of Lebanon's intervention band, dealers said. 

 The central bank widened its bid-offer intervention band to 1,551-1,559 Lebanese pounds per dollar from 1,552-1,559 on the previous Friday. 

 "Interbank trade was very light during the week. Nothing to mention," Wadih Sabbagh, chief dealer at Byblos Bank said. 

 This was due to the market quieting down after the installation of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri's new government and to the economic situation, he said. 

 "As there is no speculation, the market was left to commercial transactions. And most merchants say they have no deals because there are no commercial transactions," Sabbagh added. 

 Talal Abou Zaki, foreign exchange manager at Bank of Beirut and the Arab Countries, said there was slight dollar demand on Monday, but banks offered dollars for the rest of the week. 

 The market traded at 1,552.5-1,553.5 on Monday, but the spread narrowed by the end of the week to 25 piastres or even 15 piastres, Abou Zaki said. 

 "Today, I gave quotes to some banks for 1,551.10-1,551.25," he said. 

 He believed the central bank intervened on Wednesday and Thursday to buy dollars at 1,551.50. 

 "I don't think there is going to be much change in the market or in the central bank's intervention policy in the near future because we have got over the worst -- the change of government and all that," Abou Zaki said.

title: Bank of  Lebanon  changes  forex intervention  method.
text:
BEIRUT, Sept 26 (Reuter) - The Bank of Lebanon has changed its intervention mechanism on the Beirut foreign exchange market by shifting from a single mid-price quotation to a bid-offer system, foreign exchange dealers said on Thursday. 

 The Bank has since Tuesday set a difference of three Lebanese pounds between the prices at which it intervenes to buy and sell dollars, the dealers said. 

 This replaces a single mid-price at which it either bought or sold dollars in the past, depending on the market. 

 Dealers said the change would stimulate interbank trading, making the market less dependent on the central bank and more on supply and demand. 

 "This gives us dealers the opportunity to quote between each other. I believe it's very good," Wadih Sabbagh, chief foreign exchange dealer at Byblos Bank, told Reuters. 

 The central bank offered on Thursday to buy dollars at 1,557 pounds and to sell at 1,560. The dollar closed at 1,558.75. 

 Sabbagh said the Forex Club-Liban had asked central bank governor Riad Salameh nine months ago to set buying and selling prices to allow a spread for foreign exchange dealers to quote, and the World Bank had recommended the change. 

 "We expected this earlier, but now they have responded," Sabbagh said. 

 The central bank's practice of setting a single price for the past few years had idled Beirut dealers by making the market dependent on the Bank of Lebanon for buying and selling dollars, he said. 

 Another Beirut dealer who asked not to be identified said the Bank of Lebanon had set the band very narrow to maintain stability while giving leeway for commercial banks to make a market within those boundaries. 

 "It's not very significant because they are setting the boundaries in a very narrow band," the dealer said, "but in the longer term I think it's a step in the right direction because it will make the market more affected by supply and demand rather than just by the central bank." 

 Dealers said the central bank was taking advantage of a surge of confidence in the pound on the Beirut market during the past four weeks. 

 "I think it's a very clear sign of confidence in the pound," the dealer said. 

 He said investors were selling dollars to buy pounds, but if tension developed in the system the central bank would narrow the band. 

 "But I think with time, if we remain in a stable scenario, the band will tend to widen....Bit by bit we are moving more towards supply and demand in the interbank market." 

 -- Andrew Tarnowski - Beirut editorial (961 1) 602057 353078

title: Lebanese buy dollars as Israeli blitz continues.
text:
BEIRUT, April 16 (Reuter) - Lebanon's central bank faced demand for dollars on Tuesday because of Israel's six-day blitz on the country, but the Lebanese pound held steady at 1,581.5 to the dollar with the help of central bank intervention, dealers said. 

 "In Lebanon, the political situation always manifests itself on the foreign exchange market," a banker told Reuters. 

 Dealers who asked not to be identified estimated that the Bank of Lebanon sold between $50 million and $70 million to institutions and individuals exchanging Lebanese pounds. 

 This contrasted with the more usual pattern in recent weeks of the Bank buying up to $10 million a day to meet demand for Lebanese pounds from customers investing in high-yielding Lebanese treasury bills. 

 Tuesday's rate of 1,581.5 Lebanese pounds to the dollar was unchanged from last Thursday when the Israeli blitz began and the market closed for the four-day Greek Orthodox Easter weekend. 

 The central bank's net foreign exchange reserves currently stand at a record level of about $3 billion and a banking source said it was able to meet the demand "pretty easily." 

 "But the scope, length and term of the crisis, nobody can tell," the source said. 

 Dealers said there was no panic on the market. "The Bank of Lebanon has been intervening in a very good way, selling and buying at 1,581.5 pounds to the dollar. 

 "So the exchange rate is not being affected because the Bank can control it," a dealer told Reuters. 

 The Lebanese pound has appreciated steadily against the dollar since billionaire construction tycoon Rafik al-Hariri became prime minister in October 1992, vowing to rebuild the country from the 1975-90 civil war. 

 Political crises in the past three-and-a-half years have regularly caused runs on the pound but the central bank has defended it each time and averted any depreciation of the currency. 

 - Andrew Tarnowski, Beirut editorial (961 1) 864148 353078

title: Bank of Lebanon to continue defending pound.
text:
BEIRUT, Sept 16 (Reuter) - Lebanon's central bank will continue its policy of defending the Lebanese pound on the Beirut foreign exchange market, Bank of Lebanon governor Riad Salameh was quoted on Saturday as saying. 

 "The Bank will stay in the foreign exchange market to defend the Lebanese pound's exchange rate," as-Safir daily quoted Salameh as saying at a meeting on Friday with officials of Lebanon's Banks Association grouping Beirut's 82 banks. 

 Salameh's remark came a day after a grouping of Lebanese businessmen said in a report that the Bank should stop intervening regularly on the foreign exchange market as soon as possible to allow for a real market to emerge. 

 The Bank of Lebanon often intervenes on the market selling U.S. dollars to defend the pound, especially in times of political crisis which usually witness a flight from the local to the American currency. 

 The policy of defending the pound depleted the central bank's net foreign exchange reserves by more than $1 billion between January and June. 

 Asked about the usefulness of such a policy that was depleting the Bank's reserves, Salameh replied: 

 "I am not afraid of more defence of the pound if the 1996 public budget comes out as it should come out, especially as there will be remittances (from abroad) that have begun to flow again". 

 Salameh said there was an agreement with the ministry of finance on lowering all items in the 1996 budget draft "so that the deficit would not exceed 40 percent for any reason". 

 He said he was relieved for the disappearance of selling pressure on the pound witnessed recently. The run was caused by a political crisis between Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri that was solved last week. 

 In a second step to boost the pound, Salameh said he was in contact with the ministries of finance, and economy and trade, to take measures forcing merchants to use the local currency in transactions.

title: Lebanon Bank urged to alter  forex  policy.
text:
BEIRUT, Sept 15 (Reuter) - Lebanon's central bank should stop intervening regularly on the Beirut foreign exchange market as soon as possible to allow for a real market to emerge, Lebanese businessmen said in a report. 

 "The central bank should at the first available chance re-orient its current policy to allow for a market that reflects the reality of supply and demand in the (foreign exchange) market," the Lebanese Businessmen's Association report said. 

 An LBA delegation handed a copy of the report to billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri on Thursday. 

 The central bank, Bank of Lebanon, often intervenes on the foreign exchange market to defend the Lebanese pound, especially in times of political crisis which usually witness a flight from the local currency to U.S. dollars. 

 The policy of defending the Lebanese pound depleted the Bank's net foreign exchange reserves by more that $1 billion between January and June.

title: Top banker urges Lebanese to defend  currency .
text:
BEIRUT, Sept 11 (Reuter) - A top Lebanese banker urged the Lebanese to have confidence in their leaders and work together to maintain the value of the Lebanese pound. 

 "We must have confidence in our leaders in order to preserve the pound," Francois Bassile, president of the Banks Association, told reporters after a weekend meeting with acting Finance Minister Fouad Siniora. 

 "The value of the currency cannot be preserved by a single man but by the effort of all the Lebanese and their confidence in the government," he was quoted by newspapers as saying. 

 Basile's remarks followed the settlement last week of the latest political crisis between Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and his chief rival, parliament Speaker Nabih Berri which caused a brief flight from the pound by some Lebanese who took refuge in dollars. 

 Maintaining the stability of the currency since he took power in October 1992 is widely seen as the foremost achievement of the billionaire Hariri. 

 The pound has come under pressure several times this year due to political crises, economic uncertainties and concern about labour unrest but determined central bank intervention to sell dollars has maintained its steady appreciation against the U.S. dollar. 

 However, the interventions have helped reduce the Bank of Lebanon's foreign exchange reserves to less than $1.5 billion from $2.7 billion last December and Lebanon has experienced a net foreign exchange outflow during the year. 

 Economists and politicians have also expressed concern that the large budget deficit -- which currently shows a shortfall of more than 50 percent of income against expenditure -- is inflationary and could also undermine the currency. 

 Bassile said after his talks with Siniora that he was now convinced that measures had been taken to improve public finances and that Berri and Hariri had agreed that in future they will settle their differences through dialogue. 

 - Beirut editorial (961 1) 864148 602056 353078 861723

title: Lebanon reserves fall for sixth successive month.
text:
BEIRUT, Aug 3 (Reuter) - Central bank net foreign reserves fell $44 million in June to $1.654 billion from $1.698 billion in May, the Bank of Lebanon said on Thursday in its new monthly report. 

 It was the sixth successive month net reserves have declined, after strong growth in 1994. 

 It brought Lebanon's loss of foreign exchange reserves in the year to date to $1.078 billion, according to Bank figures. 

 The fall was due to the central bank's continued financing of public sector imports for infrastructure rehabilitation. 

 The Bank of Lebanon said the fall in reserves in June was due to its continued financing of public sector imports for infrastructure rehabilitation. The BoP shortfall that month was "largely due to a high level of public and private imports." 

 Net foreign reserves fell sharply by $550 million in May due to a run on the Lebanese pound that month caused by political and economic uncertainties, which prompted the Bank to intervene in the market to support the local currency. 

Lebanon's economic activity registered a tiny improvement in June for the fourth consecutive month, the Bank said, due to the continued expansion in the construction and transportation sectors, as well as imports. 

 The central bank's coincident indicator of economic activity rose slightly in June to 156.9 from 156.8 a month earlier. 

 Lebanon's exports were 117 billion pounds ($72 million) in June, up from 95 billion in May and 38.66 percent up on a year earlier, the Bank said. Imports rose slightly to 480 billion pounds in June from 478 billion in May and registered a 42.4 percent rise on 1994. 

 The Bank said Lebanon's external debt rose $4.5 million in June to $851.8 million from $847.3 million at the end of May. Net domestic debt reached 8,094 billion Lebanese pounds up from 7,753 billion at the end of May.

title: Lebanese pound under renewed selling pressure.
text:
BEIRUT, May 18 (Reuter) - The Lebanese pound came under renewed selling pressure on Thursday after remarks by political leaders in a dispute over presidential elections due in November, dealers said. 

 "There was demand for dollars today due to the political tension resulting from yesterday's statements," Wadih Sabbagh, chief dealer at Byblos Bank, told Reuters. 

 The selling revived pressure on the pound which has already cost the central bank nearly $300 million and aroused concern among dealers who say the next few days will be critical for the currency. 

 A dealer who declined to be named said the central bank sold $35 million on Thursday to meet demand for the U.S. currency. A second dealer put the figure nearer $45 million. 

 Beirut bankers estimate that the central bank has sold up to $280 million in the past three weeks to cover a run on the pound caused by uncertainty over the election and economic and social pressures, including a teachers' strike. 

 "There is no panic in the market but the next days are critical," Sabbagh said. 

 The pound closed unchanged at 1,627 to the dollar for the third day running after strengthening earlier thanks to the Bank of Lebanon's intervention. 

 In the political dispute Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri said on Wednesday he wants parliament to amend the constitution this month to allow a renewal or extension of President Elias Hrawi's term or to let army chief General Emile Lahoud to run for president. 

 But Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri said he wants to delay any amendments to October -- a step Hariri said his government will oppose as it keeps Lebanon in a state of uncertainty. 

 Nabil Chaya, treasurer at Credit Lyonnais Liban, said the central bank has enough reserves -- about $2.4 billion -- to meet demand for dollars but warned against a prolonged political dispute over the elections. 

 "The tension remains...Any political crisis in Lebanon has to be short-lived so as not to have an adverse effect on the financial situation, especially the foreign exchange rate of the pound," Chaya said.
